name: California
housing_duty: A housing element is mandatory under §65302(c), with detailed substantive requirements in §65583.
plan_mandate: Every city and county must adopt a general plan; charter cities must include its mandatory elements.
coverage: All cities and counties, including charter cities; no population cutoff.
assessment_detail: California HCD determines each region’s existing and projected housing need in consultation with its council of governments. Cities and counties separately assess local housing conditions and needs in their elements, but that local analysis must include the allocated regional share.
assessment_method: The statutory RHNA process governs HCD’s regional determination and the subsequent allocation, with statutory allocation objectives. Section 65583 prescribes the separate local assessment of population, employment, household characteristics, special needs and constraints.
assessment_local_role: The locality prepares and adopts its housing element, quantifies local needs and identifies sites and programs to accommodate its regional share. Local diagnosis does not replace the external RHNA number.
allocation_authority: Councils of governments; HCD where no COG
allocation_detail: HCD determines regional need; councils of governments allocate municipal/county shares, or HCD does so where no council exists. Income-specific RHNA informs land capacity and programs, not a guarantee of construction. Seventh-cycle allocations separately identify acutely low and extremely low incomes.
enforcement: HCD reviews drafts and adopted elements, may revoke compliance findings and refer violations to the Attorney General; courts can order compliance and impose escalating remedies under §65585.
key_distinction: RHNA is an external allocation of planning need. Quantified program objectives may differ from total need (§65583(b)(2)); this does not eliminate the adequate-sites obligation.

contents: Housing needs (required): Existing/projected need, household conditions, employment trends and special needs. | Income groups (required): Needs and programs across income levels; seventh-cycle additions include acutely low income households. | Land / sites inventory (required): Inventory of vacant and realistically redevelopable residential sites; relate zoning, services and fair housing to sites. | Land capacity (required): Identify adequate sites; rezone when inventory cannot accommodate assigned need. | Development constraints (required): Analyze governmental and market constraints and responses. | Fair housing (required): Fair-housing assessment, priorities, metrics and actions. | Preservation (required): At-risk assisted housing and preservation programs. | Action program (required): Scheduled actions, responsible officials and quantified objectives. | Monitoring (required): Annual progress report due April 1 covers housing-element implementation, regional-need progress, applications, approvals, entitlements, permits, occupancy and rezoned sites. Additional replacement/demolition reporting begins with the April 1, 2027 report.

name: Texas
housing_duty: No express municipal housing element duty in Chapter 213. A municipality can include housing by local choice.
plan_mandate: A municipality may adopt a comprehensive plan and determines its contents and its relationship to development regulations.
coverage: General municipal planning authority statewide; no population cutoff for a housing component appears in Chapter 213.
assessment_detail: Chapter 213 identifies no required municipal housing-need estimate or institution responsible for producing one. Its local comprehensive-plan authorization does not establish that cities actually assess housing need.
assessment_method: The municipality defines plan content and design under §213.002; Chapter 213 prescribes no housing-need formula, dataset or state-calculated planning total.
assessment_local_role: A municipality may choose to study housing in its plan. The reviewed chapter requires neither that optional analysis nor accommodation of an externally assigned housing number.
allocation_detail: Chapter 213 delegates plan contents to municipalities; it neither calculates statewide housing need nor apportions units to individual municipalities.
enforcement: Chapter 213 provides public hearing and planning-department/commission review procedures for adopted plans; no housing-element certification or housing allocation enforcement appears there.
key_distinction: Optional comprehensive planning is only one reason for this code: the operative content provisions themselves leave housing unspecified. This is not a conclusion about every HUD, land-bank, or housing-finance program.
sources: Tex. Loc. Gov’t Code §§ 213.001–.005: https://tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/LG/pdf/LG.213.pdf

name: Florida
housing_duty: The comprehensive plan must contain a housing element.
plan_mandate: Each local government must maintain a comprehensive plan; a new municipality must adopt one within three years of incorporation.
coverage: Incorporated municipalities and counties; no population cutoff for housing. The county plan controls a newly incorporated municipality until its own plan is adopted.
assessment_detail: Each local government prepares or commissions the housing-needs analysis for current and future residents, including projected households by size, income and age. State population projections are inputs, not a state housing-needs assessment assigned to the city.
assessment_method: Section 163.3177 specifies housing data and requires professionally accepted methods. Population projections may come from the Office of Economic and Demographic Research or a professionally acceptable local method; state medium projections set a minimum land-accommodation baseline, with proportional county-growth safeguards.
assessment_local_role: Translate demographic projections into local household and housing needs and adopt the housing element. The state-data and growth-floor requirements constrain inputs but do not supply a California-style municipal housing-unit allocation.
allocation_detail: Local housing-needs analysis derives household projections by income, size and age from population projections. State demographic data and a county-proportional growth floor constrain planning, but the reviewed sections do not allocate regional housing-unit need to each municipality.
enforcement: The plan must specify monitoring and implementation procedures. This inventory codes planning duties, not a guarantee of housing construction.
key_distinction: Housing-unit needs are locally analyzed; the state population-projection framework is not California's income-specific municipal allocation system.
sources: Fla. Stat. §163.3167(1)–(3): https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/163.3167 | Fla. Stat. §163.3177(1)(d), (1)(f), (6)(f): https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/163.3177
contents: Housing needs (required): Housing stock, condition, tenure, costs and cost burdens; projected households and minimum current/future housing need. | Income groups (required): Adequate sites for workforce, very-low-, low- and moderate-income housing and special housing types. | Preservation (required): Substandard conditions, rehabilitation, historic housing and preservation of affordability. | Action program (required): Housing programs; partnerships, streamlined permitting and reduced affordable-housing costs/delays. | Other content (required): Adequate future housing sites and infrastructure are required, but this is not an express parcel-by-parcel sites inventory.

name: New York
housing_duty: Existing housing resources and future housing needs, including affordable housing, are expressly optional plan topics.
plan_mandate: General city, town and village enabling statutes expressly encourage, but do not require, preparation and adoption of a comprehensive plan.
coverage: General City Law §28-a applies to cities with population no greater than one million and excludes New York City. Town Law §272-a and Village Law §7-722 apply to those municipal types. NYC's local charter planning is a separate regime, not a general statewide housing-element mandate.
assessment_detail: The reviewed general city, town and village planning statutes make housing resources and future housing needs optional plan topics. They do not require a housing-needs estimate or designate a mandatory assessor.
assessment_method: No mandatory housing-needs calculation method appears in these optional comprehensive-plan provisions. This finding does not imply that state housing research or voluntary local studies do not exist.
assessment_local_role: Local legislative/planning bodies may include housing analysis in an optional plan; that discretion is not coded as a mandatory local assessment. The general city provision excludes cities over one million.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: The reviewed city, town and village planning statutes do not assign municipal housing-unit need. They permit consideration of regional needs and local housing resources.
enforcement: Once adopted, municipal land-use regulations must accord with the plan; adoption also triggers procedural review. These effects do not make the optional housing topic mandatory.
key_distinction: A mandatory zoning-consistency rule is different from a duty to adopt a housing element. S2084 remained in Assembly committee when checked.
uncertainties: NYC's special/local planning and fair-housing obligations are not exhaustively coded; the classification describes the state general municipal planning statutes.

Town Law §272-a(1)(h), (3)(h), (11): https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/TWN/272-A | N.Y. Village Law §7-722(1)(h), (3)(h), (11): https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/VIL/7-722 | N.Y. contents: Housing needs (encouraged): Existing housing resources and future need, including affordability, may be included. | Action program (encouraged): Optional measures/programs to carry out plan objectives.

name: Pennsylvania
housing_duty: A municipal, multimunicipal or county comprehensive plan must include a plan to meet present and anticipated residents' housing needs.
plan_mandate: Municipalities governed by the Municipalities Planning Code may adopt a comprehensive plan. Counties have a separate adoption duty.
coverage: Municipalities under the MPC: cities of second class A and third class, boroughs, incorporated towns and townships. The MPC does not govern first- and second-class cities (Philadelphia and Pittsburgh); their special regimes are outside this classification.
assessment_detail: The municipal planning agency studies housing and growth for a municipal plan. Municipalities may instead prepare a joint plan, or request county planning-agency preparation, addressing housing needs across the agreed planning region.
assessment_method: MPC §§301(a)(2.1), 301.2 and 1103 require housing-needs planning and surveys of housing, demographic and economic trends. No state numerical housing-needs formula was identified in these provisions; county consistency and consultation requirements still apply.
assessment_local_role: A municipality electing to plan, or participating in a multimunicipal plan, develops the needs analysis individually or cooperatively and adopts the resulting plan. Joint regional housing analysis is distinct from a state-imposed municipal allocation.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: The MPC requires assessment of present and anticipated local residents. Joint plans may accommodate uses across the participating area; the reviewed MPC provisions do not create state-assigned municipal housing-need numbers.
enforcement: Public adoption and county/neighbor consultation; plans generally guide decisions. Section 303(c) bars invalidating an action solely for inconsistency with the plan.
key_distinction: The housing component is compulsory in an adopted comprehensive plan, while municipal plan adoption itself is generally permissive under the MPC.
uncertainties: Philadelphia and Pittsburgh's special planning laws have not been comprehensively reviewed; this row classifies the general MPC framework.
sources: Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, Act 247 of 1968, §§301(a)(2.1), 301.2–301.4, 302, 303, 1103: https://www.legis.state.pa.us/WU01/LI/LI/US/HTM/1968/0/0247..HTM
contents: Housing needs (required): Housing/demographic/economic studies and a plan for present/future housing needs. | Income groups (encouraged): Housing types and densities across incomes are listed as permissible means of addressing need. | Preservation (encouraged): Conservation of sound housing and rehabilitation of declining neighborhoods are illustrative optional measures. | Action program (required): Discuss short- and long-range implementation strategies.

name: Illinois
housing_duty: Non-exempt local governments must adopt an affordable housing plan. Newly non-exempt governments have 18 months after IHDA notification.
plan_mandate: The Affordable Housing Planning and Appeal Act imposes a separate affordable housing plan regardless of whether the municipality elects a comprehensive plan.
coverage: Municipalities with population at least 1,000 and less than 10% affordable year-round housing, as determined by IHDA; counties also covered. Municipalities under 1,000 or with at least 10% affordable housing are exempt.
assessment_detail: IHDA calculates existing affordable housing stock and the affordable share for each local government to determine exemption status. A non-exempt local government’s plan must state the affordable units necessary to reach exemption and address local constraints and implementation. This is a stock/exemption benchmark, not a state forecast of total or regional future housing need.
assessment_method: Sections 15 and 20 prescribe IHDA’s formula using Census and other relevant data: affordable owner units below 80% and rental units below 60% of county or metropolitan median household income, divided by total year-round housing units. Section 25 requires the local plan’s exemption-unit statement and supplies alternative statutory goals. IHDA’s additional income-band data are informational and do not determine exemptions.
assessment_local_role: The local government adopts the affordable housing plan, states its exemption-related unit requirement using the statutory benchmark, identifies sites/constraints/incentives, and chooses one or more §25 goals. It can appeal IHDA’s exemption determination under the Act; it receives no allocated share of regional future need.
allocation_authority: No regional-need allocator; statutory stock benchmarks
allocation_detail: IHDA calculates existing affordable-stock percentages. The plan selects one or more statutory goals: 15% of new development/redevelopment affordable, a 5-percentage-point increase in affordable stock, or 10% overall affordable stock. These are uniform statutory benchmarks with local choice, not an allocation of regional housing need to cities.
enforcement: IHDA determines substantial compliance and notifies violations; the Attorney General may seek mandamus, injunction, or other relief. Section 30 also provides affordable-development appeals. These mechanisms do not guarantee unit production.
key_distinction: The Act’s encouragement language in its purpose does not make the non-exempt-government duty optional. Its 10% exemption threshold and alternative goals are not California-style regional need allocation.
sources: 310 ILCS 67/25: https://ilga.gov/Documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/031000670K25.htm | 310 ILCS 67/15, /20, /30, /70: https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/ILCS/Articles?ActID=2477&ChapterID=29 | Illinois HB5198 (104th General Assembly), bill status: https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/BillStatus?DocNum=5198&DocTypeID=HB&GAID=18&LegId=166836&Print=1&SessionID=114 | IHDA, Affordable Housing Planning and Appeal Act: https://www.ihda.org/about-ihda/ahpaa/
contents: Housing needs (required): State the affordable units needed to reach exempt status. | Income groups (required): Affordability calculations distinguish owner units affordable below 80% and rental units below 60% of median household income in the county or primary metropolitan statistical area. | Land / sites inventory (required): Identify suitable land for affordable construction and structures suitable for conversion or rehabilitation; consider ownership/rental, committed developers, and public or semi-public sites. Not the detailed California parcel-capacity protocol. | Development constraints (required): Describe market conditions, infrastructure limits, ordinances and policies constraining affordable housing; devise mitigation strategies. | Fair housing (required): Constraints analysis includes policies or practices that fail to affirmatively further fair housing. | Action program (required): Identify incentives, choose statutory goal(s), and propose timelines for actions to commence within 24 months of adoption. | Monitoring (required): File the plan with IHDA within 60 days; implementation report no later than four years after adoption/update; prior plans require progress summaries.

name: Ohio
housing_duty: The reviewed municipal planning statute does not expressly require a housing element, housing needs assessment, or equivalent citywide housing plan.
plan_mandate: Section 713.01 authorizes cities and villages to establish commissions. Once established, § 713.02 directs the commission to make plans and maps.
coverage: General city/village planning-commission regime; no housing-specific population or geography trigger appears in §§ 713.01–.02. Local charter provisions may add duties.
assessment_detail: The municipal planning commission prepares physical-development plans and maps, but §713.02 identifies no required housing-need estimate or housing assessor.
assessment_method: The statute lists physical/public-facility planning topics and permits information and funding cooperation. It supplies no housing-demand calculation method or state housing total for municipal planning.
assessment_local_role: The commission performs the statutory general planning work. A municipality’s voluntary housing study is not established by that general duty; no external housing-unit number must be accommodated under the reviewed sections.
allocation_detail: The enumerated planning duties and public-project review powers in § 713.02 do not allocate state or regional housing need to municipalities.
enforcement: The statute requires commission review of specified public projects after a plan exists, with legislative overrides. No housing-element compliance or assigned-unit enforcement mechanism is identified in these provisions.
key_distinction: A duty to make municipal plans is not itself a duty to prepare a housing element; a local housing strategy or federal consolidated plan is a different instrument.
sources: Ohio Rev. Code § 713.01: https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-713.01 | Ohio Rev. Code § 713.02: https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-713.02

name: Georgia
housing_duty: Housing element required for HUD Community Development Block Grant Entitlement Communities; expressly optional and encouraged for other local governments.
plan_mandate: A comprehensive plan is required to retain qualified-local-government certification and eligibility for selected state funding and permitting programs.
coverage: The operative trigger is HUD CDBG entitlement-community status, not receipt of any federal grant. The standards operate within Georgia's qualified-local-government planning system; approved alternative planning requirements are possible.
assessment_detail: For the CDBG entitlement communities required to include housing, the local comprehensive-plan process evaluates housing-stock adequacy for current and future community needs. Existing consolidated-plan or comparable local housing-plan analysis may substitute.
assessment_method: DCA Rule 110-12-1-.03(9) prescribes factors including stock/type/condition, costs and burdens, jobs-housing balance, special populations and life-cycle options. The reviewed rule does not prescribe a state-calculated unit-need total.
assessment_local_role: Prepare or incorporate the local housing analysis and integrate applicable goals, needs and work-program items into the comprehensive plan. Regional/state review of that plan is not the same as calculating and allocating municipal housing need.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: Evaluate local housing-stock adequacy and current/future needs. The reviewed rules prescribe no state or regional assignment of a municipal housing-unit share.
enforcement: Regional Commission and Department of Community Affairs review for conformity; certification determines eligibility for selected funding and permitting programs.
key_distinction: The required analysis inventories existing housing stock; it does not prescribe a parcel-level inventory of developable sites.
sources: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 110-12-1-.02; -.03(9): https://rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/110-12-1
contents: Housing needs (required): Evaluate housing mix, condition, occupancy, costs, cost-burdened households and jobs–housing balance. | Income groups (required): Affordability/cost burdens, special populations and housing across the life cycle. | Action program (required): Integrate housing-related goals, needs/opportunities and work-program actions into the comprehensive plan even when using a Consolidated Plan analysis.

name: North Carolina
housing_duty: Housing plans and a comprehensive-plan topic covering diverse housing types and affordability are expressly optional under the general enabling statute.
plan_mandate: A local government must adopt and reasonably maintain a comprehensive or land-use plan as a condition of exercising zoning authority.
coverage: General framework applies to local governments exercising Chapter 160D zoning authority; no population trigger for the optional housing topic. Coastal CAMA land-use planning has additional rules and is treated separately in the caveat.
assessment_detail: Section 160D-501 permits housing plans and housing-affordability topics but does not require a housing-needs estimate or name a mandatory housing-needs assessor.
assessment_method: The reviewed general-planning statute sets no mandatory housing-need calculation method. Its optional housing topic concerns types and affordability; the separate coastal stock-inventory access caveat remains.
assessment_local_role: A local government may undertake housing analysis within its plan, which is adopted with planning-board advice. That optional analysis is not treated as a state-mandated local need assessment.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: The reviewed general planning statute creates no state/regional allocation of municipal housing-unit need.
enforcement: Adoption is a condition of zoning authority. Plans are advisory without independent regulatory effect, and must be considered when amending zoning.
key_distinction: Mandatory adoption of some plan does not make every suggested topic mandatory. Coastal land-use rules additionally require housing-stock information; stock description is not a housing-needs allocation.
uncertainties: The official coastal-rule server could not be fully retrieved. Secondary indexed text of 15A NCAC 07B .0702 identifies mandatory coastal-plan housing-stock estimates; this has not been elevated to a source-checked housing-element mandate.
sources: N.C. Gen. Stat. §160D-501(a)–(c), §160D-503: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/ByArticle/Chapter_160D/Article_5.html
contents: Income groups (encouraged): A plan may address housing types and affordability for all household types and income levels. | Housing needs (encouraged): Optional separate housing plan and general needs analysis.

name: Michigan
housing_duty: Master plans must include an assessment of existing and forecast housing demands, with responsive strategies and policies, among subjects reasonably pertinent to future development. This express housing provision took effect April 2, 2025.
plan_mandate: The Planning Enabling Act authorizes a local government to adopt a master plan and create a planning commission; once constituted, the commission shall make and approve a plan. This is not a universal municipal housing-element mandate.
coverage: No population cutoff in the housing provision. Applies through the master-plan framework and its pertinence qualification. Plans carried forward from repealed planning acts are exempt from §33 contents until first amended under the 2008 act.
assessment_detail: The local planning commission prepares the master plan, including an assessment of the community’s existing and forecast housing demands and responsive policies, subject to the statutory pertinence qualification and older-plan exception.
assessment_method: The Planning Enabling Act requires the assessment and strategies but does not specify a statewide numerical housing-needs formula in the reviewed provisions. Its procedural and content requirements still constrain plan preparation.
assessment_local_role: The commission assesses community housing demands and incorporates strategies into the master plan. No state or regional housing-unit number that the municipality must accommodate was identified in the reviewed act.
allocation_detail: The statute calls for an assessment of the community's own housing demands. No state or regional assignment of municipal unit needs was identified in the reviewed Planning Enabling Act.
enforcement: The act prescribes plan adoption, intergovernmental notice and periodic review. No housing-specific state certification, assigned unit quota or housing-production sanction was identified in this act.
key_distinction: Michigan now expressly requires a housing-demand assessment in applicable master plans; a claim that its planning act is silent on housing misses the 2025-effective amendment.
sources: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 125.3807, .3811, .3831, .3833(2)(e), .3845(2), .3881(1): https://www.legislature.mi.gov/documents/mcl/pdf/mcl-Act-33-of-2008.pdf
contents: Housing needs (required): Assess existing and forecast community housing demands, subject to the statutory pertinence qualification. | Action program (required): Strategies and policies to address those demands; the plan also includes implementation recommendations. | Monitoring (required): Review the master plan at least every five years and record whether amendment or replacement should begin; this is plan review rather than a housing-production reporting duty.

name: New Jersey
housing_duty: Municipalities exercising ordinary zoning authority need a housing plan element; municipalities using the statutory fair-share compliance process must adopt the element and fair share plan on the statutory schedule.
plan_mandate: A housing element is a prerequisite to ordinary municipal zoning under the MLUL. The Fair Housing Act provides a housing-element/fair-share-plan process for obtaining protection against exclusionary-zoning suits; participation in that compliance process is voluntary, while the underlying fair-share obligation is not.
coverage: No housing-element population cutoff. Statewide fair-share obligations, with qualified urban-aid municipalities exempt from prospective need (not automatically from present need). Urban-aid eligibility requires designated state aid plus deficient-housing ratio above the regional ratio, density above 10,000/square mile, or density above 6,000 but below 10,000 and a statutory vacant-parcel measure below 5%.
assessment_detail: DCA calculates regional low- and moderate-income need and municipal present/prospective obligations. Each municipality determines its own obligation under the same statutory formulas; the dispute-resolution program or courts can adjust the determination. Municipal housing elements also analyze local stock, demographics and capacity.
assessment_method: Sections 52:27D-304.2–304.3 prescribe regional and municipal formulas and relevant datasets. DCA's published calculations are expressly nonbinding; that does not make the statutory formula optional.
assessment_local_role: Adopt a binding resolution explaining the municipality's calculation, subject to challenge and program/court resolution, then prepare a housing element and fair-share plan for the resulting obligation. Separate local analysis does not permit unilateral disregard of the statutory fair share.
allocation_authority: State statutory formula; municipal determination, subject to program/courts
allocation_detail: Yes: regional low/moderate-income prospective need is allocated by a statutory average of nonresidential-valuation, income-capacity and land-capacity factors. DCA publishes nonbinding municipal calculations; municipal binding resolutions and the court/dispute process establish obligations. The duty is a realistic opportunity for housing, not municipal construction.
enforcement: Compliance certification and court/dispute review; missed requirements can remove immunity from exclusionary-zoning litigation. DCA monitors units and trust funds; new monitoring rules took effect in December 2025.
key_distinction: DCA numbers are guidance, but the statutory regional fair-share formula and enforceable obligation remain. Opting out of the administrative compliance process does not erase the obligation.
uncertainties: The current NJ legislature statute viewer failed; the MLUL zoning prerequisite is documented by an adopted municipal plan on an official state server. The 2024 Fair Housing Act itself was directly reviewed.

DCA, 2025–2035 Affordable Housing Calculations: https://nj.gov/dca/dlps/4th_Round_Numbers.shtml | N.J. DCA, Fair Share Plan Preparation and Model Documents: https://www.nj.gov/dca/dlps/hss/planresources.shtml | N.J. contents: Housing needs (required): Housing-stock inventory and ten-year projection; household demographics and employment. | Income groups (required): Present/prospective low- and moderate-income fair share; very-low-income requirements apply within the affordable program. | Land / sites inventory (required): Consider land suitable for affordable construction and structures for conversion/rehabilitation, including committed developers' land. | Land capacity (required): Assess capacity to accommodate present/prospective need; special redevelopment analysis when claiming a vacant-land adjustment. | Development constraints (required): Evaluate ordinances/local factors affecting multigenerational family continuity. | Action program (required): Realistic-opportunity demonstration, implementing ordinances, prior-round obligations and trust-fund spending plan where applicable. | Monitoring (required): State reporting of affordable units and municipal trust funds.

name: Virginia
housing_duty: The plan must designate areas and implementation measures for affordable housing sufficient for current and future residents across income levels.
plan_mandate: Every local governing body must adopt a comprehensive plan.
coverage: All localities, including cities and towns; no housing-component population cutoff. Population triggers for other topics, such as transit-oriented development, do not narrow this duty.
assessment_detail: The local planning commission assesses current and future residents' affordable housing needs through the comprehensive plan, while considering the planning district's needs. The cited law does not prescribe a separate quantified state estimate.
assessment_method: Section 15.2-2223 requires careful study of local conditions/growth and affordable-housing measures sufficient for current and future needs at all income levels. It supplies substantive criteria, without a housing-unit calculation formula in the reviewed section.
assessment_local_role: Prepare local affordable-housing areas and measures, consider district needs, and adopt the plan locally. Considering the district does not itself create an externally apportioned municipal share.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: Local need must be addressed while considering the planning district's needs. The reviewed provisions assign no externally calculated municipal unit share.
enforcement: Statutory preparation/adoption and five-year review duties. No housing-specific state certification or municipal construction quota is created by the cited provisions.
key_distinction: A functional affordable-housing component is mandatory even though the statute does not call it a separate housing element.
sources: Va. Code §15.2-2223(A), (D): https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title15.2/chapter22/section15.2-2223/ | Va. Code §15.2-2223.5: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title15.2/chapter22/section15.2-2223.5/ | Va. Code §15.2-2230: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title15.2/chapter22/section15.2-2230/
contents: Housing needs (required): Current and future local housing need; planning-district context. | Income groups (required): Residents at all income levels. | Preservation (required): Construction, rehabilitation and maintenance of affordable housing. | Action program (required): Designate areas and implementation measures; area designation is not an express parcel inventory. | Other content (required): At plan amendments after July 1, 2021, incorporate strategies promoting manufactured housing as affordable housing. | Monitoring (required): Review the comprehensive plan at least every five years to determine whether to amend.

name: Washington
housing_duty: A mandatory housing element applies to every jurisdiction required or choosing to plan under RCW36.70A.040.
plan_mandate: Counties fully planning under the Growth Management Act and every city within them must adopt comprehensive plans; counties can also opt into that system.
coverage: County-based trigger, not city size: county population ≥50,000 with >17% growth over ten years (historically >10% before May16,1995), or >20% growth regardless of size; all its cities follow. Prior qualifying status persists. Opt-in counties are covered, subject to statutory historical withdrawal exceptions; qualifying counties below50,000 may exercise the specified timely opt-out.
assessment_detail: Washington Commerce supplies countywide housing-need projections by income segment and for emergency and supportive housing. Counties coordinate municipal shares with their cities. Cities still inventory existing housing and analyze their net new needs and capacity.
assessment_method: Commerce provides the housing-need projection model and technical guidance. The model uses a locally selected population projection; county/city allocation must preserve at least the projected countywide need for each economic segment and follow applicable countywide or multicounty policies.
assessment_local_role: Counties and cities select the population input, coordinate local shares, and prepare local needs and capacity analyses. City plans use the resulting allocation; cities may plan for more capacity with supporting infrastructure and coordination.
allocation_authority: Counties coordinating with cities and towns
allocation_detail: Commerce supplies countywide need projections by income and special housing category. Counties coordinate city/town shares through countywide planning; WAC365-196-410 requires consistent public allocations whose sum covers countywide need. Applicable fully planning municipalities must show sufficient capacity for their assigned need.
enforcement: GMA compliance includes plan/development-regulation review. The 2025 Housing Accountability Act adds Commerce selected/voluntary housing reviews; noncompliance can restrict denials of affordable/moderate-income projects and eligibility for state funding.
key_distinction: State projections are allocated through county/city coordination, not a single state formula that directly fixes every city's share. Land-capacity analysis is explicit; no universal California-style parcel schedule is coded from these provisions.

name: Arizona
housing_duty: Cities of at least 50,000 must include a housing element. Separately, nontribal municipalities of at least 30,000 must publish housing needs assessments and an annual plan to address identified needs.
plan_mandate: Each municipality must adopt a comprehensive long-range general plan (§9-461.05(A)).
coverage: Housing element: cities ≥50,000; optional below that threshold. Separate assessment/report: municipalities ≥30,000, excluding municipalities on tribal land; five-year assessments and annual reports began January 1, 2025.
assessment_detail: The municipality identifies and analyzes existing and forecast housing needs in its general-plan housing element. Under the separately applicable assessment statute, it publishes five-year population/job projections and estimates additional rental and ownership units needed for existing deficits and growth across incomes.
assessment_method: Sections9-461.05(E)(6) and9-469 prescribe subjects and required inputs, including population, jobs, zoning acreage and housing deficits. They do not supply an external municipal unit calculation. The Arizona Department of Housing compiles local annual reports rather than calculating the controlling local need under these provisions.
assessment_local_role: The municipality produces the needs assessment and its response plan under the relevant population thresholds. No externally allocated regional number was identified; §9-469(E) expressly says the municipality need not fulfill the projections.
allocation_detail: Municipalities estimate additional rental/ownership need using population, jobs, existing deficits and income levels. The reviewed statutes supply no externally assigned municipal share; §9-469(E) expressly disclaims a duty to fulfill projections.
enforcement: Annual housing reports go to Arizona Department of Housing for compilation and legislative/executive transmission. §9-469(E) does not require actual fulfillment of projected need.
key_distinction: Two thresholds: 50,000 for the named element, 30,000 for the separate planning/reporting duty. Adequate sites and aggregate zoned acreage do not establish a California-style parcel inventory.

contents: Housing needs (required): Existing/forecasted needs in the element; five-year population/jobs and additional-unit needs in the separate assessment. | Income groups (required): Element addresses every economic segment; assessment covers needs across incomes. | Land capacity (required): Housing element requires provision of adequate sites; no express parcel inventory in the cited provisions. | Preservation (required): Standards/programs to eliminate substandard conditions and improve housing quality. | Fair housing (required): Equal provision regardless of race, color, creed or economic level. | Action program (required): Annual report includes a plan for satisfying identified additional-unit needs. | Monitoring (required): Report development applications, approvals and production stages, plus progress. | Other content (required): Separate assessment reports aggregate residentially zoned land by single-family/multifamily; this is not a developable-sites inventory.

name: Tennessee
housing_duty: Housing is expressly optional in the separate countywide growth plan under § 6-58-107(d); subsection (e)(8) states a housing-choice and affordability objective. The municipal general-plan provision does not add a required housing element.
plan_mandate: An established municipal commission has the general-plan duty stated in § 13-4-201. Separately, Chapter 58 requires a countywide growth plan and consistent local land-use decisions.
coverage: General municipal planning commissions plus the separate countywide growth-plan framework; no housing-element population cutoff identified. Private/special municipal planning acts may add requirements.
assessment_detail: Municipal general planning and countywide growth planning identify no separately required housing-need estimate or housing assessor. The growth plan’s broad future-needs and affordability objectives coexist with expressly optional substantive housing treatment.
assessment_method: Section 13-4-201 prescribes physical-development and service-area analysis. Section 6-58-107 makes a housing topic optional and states housing-choice/affordability goals; neither provision specifies a housing-unit formula or a state-calculated municipal housing total. Existing source-access limitations remain.
assessment_local_role: Local officials may analyze housing when preparing the optional housing portion of a county growth plan or municipal plan. General growth-boundary planning and adoption do not establish a required housing-demand calculation or external housing-unit allocation.
allocation_detail: Future growth and affordability are planning objectives; the reviewed provisions do not assign state or regional housing-unit shares to municipalities.
enforcement: Section 6-58-107 requires local land-use decisions to be consistent with an approved growth plan. Neither that section nor § 13-4-201 supplies a housing-element certification or assigned-unit enforcement system.
key_distinction: Tennessee’s affordability objective should not disappear from a negative coding. The statute expressly makes substantive housing treatment optional, and the TACIR staff report explains that distinction; this is not a finding of no housing-related policy in state law.
uncertainties: Current official annotated-code section text was not extracted; a final current official text check should confirm the 2025 mirror before publication as independently validated law. | The growth-plan affordability objective is a policy requirement, while the detailed housing element is optional. This classification uses the latter as the comparable municipal housing-element measure.

name: Massachusetts
housing_duty: Section 81D master plans must include a housing element. A separate Chapter 40B Housing Production Plan is an optional route to permit-appeal safe harbor.
plan_mandate: A planning board established under Chapter 41 §81A shall make a master plan, which may cover the city/town or parts the board considers advisable.
coverage: Section 81D applies to §81A planning boards. Section 81A permits cities except Boston and towns to establish boards; towns reaching 10,000 inhabitants without a planning board must establish one. A town below 10,000 may authorize selectmen to act as the planning board. Boston is outside this general-law framework.
assessment_detail: The §81A planning board identifies and analyzes existing and forecast housing needs in its §81D master plan. Separate MBTA zoning and Chapter 40B HPP stock-based benchmarks do not make the state the assessor of the master plan's housing need.
assessment_method: Section 81D(3) specifies needs analysis, objectives and housing programs but no numerical state need-allocation formula. HPP production benchmarks use existing housing stock; MBTA district requirements are a separate zoning mechanism.
assessment_local_role: Develop and adopt the master-plan housing analysis locally. Cities may pursue the separate HPP process and covered communities must meet applicable MBTA zoning duties, but neither is an assigned share of regional master-plan housing need.
allocation_authority: No regional-need allocator identified; separate state zoning/HPP benchmarks
allocation_detail: The master-plan housing assessment is local. Separate MBTA Communities law requires qualifying as-of-right multifamily districts; Chapter 40B HPP certification uses a 0.5% annual subsidized-housing benchmark based on existing stock. These are zoning/production benchmarks, not an assignment of regional housing need to every municipality.
enforcement: Section 81D requires public-record plans and submission to the state housing office but sets no fixed adoption deadline. HPP safe harbor requires state approval and certification of production; MBTA noncompliance affects specified state funding.
key_distinction: Do not equate the master-plan housing element, optional 40B HPP, or mandatory MBTA multifamily zoning. They are distinct legal mechanisms.

contents: Housing needs (required): Identify/analyze existing and forecast housing needs and objectives. | Preservation (required): Programs to preserve, improve and develop housing. | Action program (required): Policies for balanced local housing opportunities; schedule actions and regulatory changes needed to implement the plan.

name: Indiana
housing_duty: No express housing element in the reviewed general-plan requirements. HEA1001 (2026) separately requires a housing-oriented review of development regulations and housing reports; those duties are not a forward-looking housing-needs plan.
plan_mandate: A plan commission prepares a comprehensive plan under §36-7-4-501. A locality exercising planning/zoning powers uses this statutory framework; no zoning ordinance may be adopted before a comprehensive plan is approved.
coverage: General local planning framework; no housing-element population cutoff because no express element was found. New regulatory review covers counties, cities and towns. Housing-progress reporting applies to units exercising planning/zoning; housing-status reporting covers all counties, cities and towns.
assessment_detail: The reviewed general-plan provisions do not require a housing-needs estimate. HEA1001 requires review of housing regulations and reports on past housing outcomes; neither creates a required forward-looking housing-needs assessor.
assessment_method: HEA1001 prescribes regulatory-review factors and reporting fields. It requires copies of specified preexisting housing studies where available, rather than commissioning a new needs calculation. IHCDA compiles reported outcomes and regional comparisons.
assessment_local_role: Undertake the required regulatory review and report local outcomes beginning around January 2027. Optional existing local/regional studies may inform that work, but no externally assigned need total must be accommodated under the reviewed provisions.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: Neither the reviewed general-plan provisions nor 2026 HEA1001 assigns municipalities quantified regional housing need. New state reporting compiles outcomes and regional comparisons; it does not distribute a building obligation.
enforcement: A comprehensive plan is a zoning prerequisite. HEA1001 requires a public regulatory-review hearing and report by January 1, 2027, plus annual housing reports beginning 2027. IHCDA's September 2026 guidance implements the one-time report by December 31, 2026 and annual reporting by January 31. These are adjacent review/reporting duties, not housing-element certification.
key_distinction: No express housing element does not mean no housing duties: HEA1001 mandates review of density, housing types, approvals and other housing reforms, and reports on local housing outcomes. It does not require adopting every reform or a California-style allocation.
timing_note: Separate housing review/report due around January 2027; no housing element identified.
uncertainties: Official current IGA code and enrolled-PDF endpoints returned an application shell. General statutory text was checked through a 2025 official municipal reproduction and 2025 mirrors, with HEA1001/SEA285 separately checked against enrolled text and official enactment status. A direct current-code verification remains desirable. | The classification excludes one-time regulatory review and backward-looking housing data reports from the definition of a housing element/equivalent needs plan. Those mandatory adjacent duties are described explicitly.

name: Missouri
housing_duty: No express housing-element requirement in the reviewed city-plan provisions. Blighted-area replanning is an optional listed subject.
plan_mandate: Municipalities may undertake city planning and appoint a commission; an appointed statutory commission shall make/adopt the city plan.
coverage: General municipal authorization in §§ 89.310–.340; no housing-specific population cutoff or mandatory municipal housing-plan class appears there.
assessment_detail: Section 89.340 directs a municipal commission to prepare the city plan but does not require a housing-need estimate or designate a housing assessor.
assessment_method: Physical-development and land-use recommendations, optional blight replanning and optional zoning plans do not provide a housing-need formula or state-calculated total.
assessment_local_role: The commission prepares general recommendations and may address additional local subjects. The reviewed municipal provisions do not require a housing-needs calculation or accommodation of external municipal housing shares.
allocation_detail: Section 89.340 supplies physical-development and optional zoning-plan authority; it creates neither a municipal fair-share calculation nor a regional allocation of needed units.
enforcement: No state housing-element review or housing allocation enforcement appears in the reviewed sections. The plan is a commission recommendation for physical development.
key_distinction: Do not treat optional blight/slum replanning, or an introduced bill proposing a housing element, as an enacted citywide housing-needs duty.

name: Maryland
housing_duty: Housing element mandatory. As of the check date, it must address affordable housing need, including workforce and low-income housing, and applicable fair-housing assessment.
plan_mandate: Local jurisdictions must adopt and execute a comprehensive plan; a municipality may participate in an approved county plan.
coverage: Municipal corporations and counties; no population cutoff. Municipal participation in a county plan is allowed by mutual resolutions. Charter counties have parallel housing-element duties.
assessment_detail: The local jurisdiction's planning process addresses its affordable housing need, including workforce and low-income housing. This is a local assessment duty; the operative provisions do not require a state-calculated numerical need total for each municipality.
assessment_method: Operative §§3-114 and 1-407.1 specify income categories and fair-housing assessment, with state technical assistance on request. The October 1, 2026 replacement adds state-plan and data inputs; those inputs do not transfer the local housing-needs assessment to the state.
assessment_local_role: Prepare and adopt the local housing element, or participate in the approved county plan where permitted, assessing local affordable need and fair housing. No externally assigned municipal number is identified.
allocation_authority: No external municipal need allocator identified
allocation_detail: Housing need is assessed within the local jurisdiction. Neither the operative housing provision nor the enacted October 2026 replacement establishes municipal numerical shares of regional housing need.
enforcement: Mandatory plan content; state technical assistance. The fair-housing subsection expressly does not prescribe or prohibit a specific local action.
key_distinction: HB243/Chapter 110 is enacted but takes effect October 1, 2026. Do not apply its expanded site/supply requirements before that date.

name: Colorado
housing_duty: Covered local governments must complete a housing-needs assessment by December 31, 2026 and a narrower subset must adopt a responsive housing action plan by January 1, 2028; both repeat at least every six years.
plan_mandate: The housing-needs assessment and housing action plan are separate statutory planning duties under Title24, part37, linked to the territory covered by local master plans.
coverage: Assessment: local governments with population at least 1,000, excluding those whose most recent decennial census population fell at least 1%, unless they receive DOLA assessment funding; a timely regional assessment substitutes. Action plan: population at least 5,000, or at least 1,000 if participating in a regional assessment or qualifying as a rural resort community as of January 1, 2024; the same 1% decline exemption applies. Population is measured two years before the relevant deadline; counties count only unincorporated population. Rural-resort communities include municipalities in counties so classified by the state. Qualifying early-2024 plans receive a five-year transition.
assessment_detail: The local government conducts a local housing-needs assessment, or a regional entity conducts a substituting regional assessment that estimates need and municipal allocations. DOLA separately must conduct a statewide assessment by November 30, 2027; that state research does not turn all local assessments into state-assigned need.
assessment_method: DOLA’s executive director develops the required assessment methodologies, data standards and displacement guidance under§3702. Local and regional assessors apply them; DOLA checks conformity. Regional methodology includes jobs-based municipal allocations, while local methodology incorporates applicable state/regional needs as appropriate.
assessment_local_role: A locality conducts and publicly considers its own assessment or participates in and comments on a regional assessment. The responsive action plan explains how any applicable regional allocation is addressed. Regional participation remains optional; first assessment and plan deadlines are separately stated.
allocation_authority: Regional assessment entity, where that optional pathway is used
allocation_detail: Optional regional assessments estimate a municipal allocation of regional housing need based on jobs and dependence on regional employment, among other factors. A local action plan must explain how it addresses any applicable regional allocation. Outside that pathway, the locality assesses its own need under state methodology and incorporates applicable state/regional needs as appropriate. This is a conditional regional planning allocation, not a statewide RHNA schedule or a construction quota.
enforcement: DOLA must reject assessments or plans lacking statutory components and reviews three-year implementation reports. Starting December 1, 2027 specified land-use/housing grant programs prioritize compliant jurisdictions, treating exempt jurisdictions as compliant. The provisions require planning and strategy review, not completion of an assigned construction count.
key_distinction: Colorado is more than a zoning-strategy menu: participating regional assessments estimate municipal need allocations. That pathway is optional, while the size-based assessment and action-plan duties have approaching statutory deadlines.
timing_note: Enacted duties: assessments due December 31, 2026; action plans due January 1, 2028. Regional participation is optional; municipal regional allocations apply where that assessment pathway is used.
sources: Colo. Rev. Stat. §§24-32-3702–3706, 24-32-3710 (2026): https://olls.info/crs/crs2026-title-24.htm | Colo. Rev. Stat. §§29-32-101(10), 29-4-1107(1)(d): https://olls.info/crs/crs2026-title-29.htm
contents: Housing needs (required): Estimate housing stock and need, households, jobs by pay, displacement risk, with consideration of shortages/surpluses, vacancy, homelessness, job–housing balance and state demographic projections. | Income groups (required): Sort need by income and dwelling type, including accessible, supportive, ownership and rental housing. Baseline categories include extremely low, very low, low, moderate and middle income. | Land capacity (required): Action plans assess existing zoning/density effects on the number and type of needed homes and opportunities for higher-density affordable housing near major transit. | Development constraints (required): Assess housing-market limitations and zoning/density effects; action plans identify recommended local-law changes. | Preservation (required): Action plans choose goals and strategies for production and preservation of affordable and regulated affordable housing. | Action program (required): Action plans select at least two standard affordability strategies, one long-term strategy and a suitable displacement strategy; include a plan for legislative consideration and an inclusive engagement process. | Monitoring (required): Plan includes available six-year construction/permitting history. Three years after adoption report actual strategy/law adoption or a good-faith effort with alternatives; repeat assessment and plan at least every six years. | Other content (required): Analyze areas or communities at elevated displacement risk and plan mitigation. These obligations do not expressly require a parcel-by-parcel available-land inventory.

name: Wisconsin
housing_duty: The comprehensive plan must include a housing element addressing existing and forecast demand, housing stock and policies for housing choice, lower-income land availability and preservation.
plan_mandate: A comprehensive plan is required for local governments enacting or amending the listed zoning, subdivision or official-mapping ordinances. City plan commissions have a master-plan function; the nine-element requirement is linked to these regulatory actions. A voluntarily adopted comprehensive plan also must contain all nine elements.
coverage: Cities, villages and towns using the land-use regulatory powers listed in §66.1001(3), with no population cutoff. The consistency requirement began January 1, 2010; §(3m) preserves historic grant-related extensions, including the now-expired January 1, 2012 exception and extensions lasting until their grant deadline.
assessment_detail: The local government assesses existing and forecast housing demand and the age, condition, value and occupancy of its own housing stock for the comprehensive-plan housing element.
assessment_method: Section66.1001 prescribes housing and demographic subjects, income/age/special-needs coverage and plan horizons, rather than a state-calculated municipal need formula. The reviewed provisions do not designate a state or regional body to supply a controlling local housing-unit need.
assessment_local_role: The locality uses its forecasts and stock analysis to adopt housing policies and programs within the comprehensive-plan framework. No external municipal allocation was identified; a regional planning commission’s comprehensive plan is expressly advisory.
allocation_detail: The element addresses the locality's existing and forecast housing demand. No externally assigned municipal housing-unit need appears in the reviewed provisions; regional comprehensive plans are expressly advisory to local governments under §66.1001(5).
enforcement: Listed regulatory enactments and amendments must be consistent with the comprehensive plan; plan adoption requires all nine elements, public participation and a hearing. No state housing-element certification or municipal unit allocation was found in these provisions.
key_distinction: The duty is tied to comprehensive planning and specified land-use powers, not a population-based universal housing quota. Enacted 2025 Act 173 changes city/village residential land and density planning and consistency rules beginning January 1, 2028; those future provisions are not treated as current inventory requirements.
sources: Wis. Stat. §66.1001(1)–(3): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/66.1001 | Wis. Stat. §66.1001(3m)–(5): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/66/x/1001/3m | Wis. Stat. §62.23(2)–(3): https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/62.23
contents: Housing needs (required): Assess existing and forecast housing demand and stock age, structure, value and occupancy. | Income groups (required): Policies and programs must serve all income levels and age groups and persons with special needs. | Preservation (required): Policies and programs to maintain or rehabilitate existing housing stock. | Action program (required): Identify housing programs, including policies promoting land availability for low- and moderate-income development or redevelopment; the plan's implementation element sequences actions. | Monitoring (required): The implementation element must describe how progress will be measured; update the comprehensive plan at least once every ten years. | Other content (required): The separate land-use element assesses land supply, demand, density and redevelopment, with 20-year projections in five-year increments and land-use maps. This is not coded as a suitable-parcel housing inventory.

name: Minnesota
housing_duty: Metropolitan comprehensive plans must include a housing element and housing implementation program.
plan_mandate: The Metropolitan Land Planning Act requires comprehensive plans and decennial review within the Metropolitan Council region. General municipal planning is governed separately by §462.355.
coverage: Metropolitan Council territory: Anoka, Carver, Dakota (excluding Northfield and Cannon Falls), Hennepin (excluding Hanover and Rockford), Ramsey, Scott (excluding New Prague), and Washington counties. No municipal population cutoff. Housing-element duty extends to communities without forecast sewer-serviced growth, although allocation/capacity requirements do not.
assessment_detail: The Metropolitan Council calculates the region’s future affordable-housing need and each applicable sewer-growth jurisdiction’s share. This future-need calculation concerns added lower-income households; it excludes existing unmet demand. Cities and townships separately assess current local and regional housing needs.
assessment_method: The Metropolitan Council sets and updates the regional methodology each planning cycle. Its 2021–2030 allocation uses forecast growth, existing affordable stock and low-wage job–worker balance. The 2031–2040 cycle focuses on housing affordable at or below 60% AMI, with lower-income bands. Council-provided Existing Housing Assessments are starting data for separate local diagnosis.
assessment_local_role: Covered localities report their future-need allocation and guide sufficient land/density where the allocation applies. They also use local knowledge to analyze existing needs and prepare implementation policies. Jurisdictions without forecast sewer-serviced growth still have housing-element duties even when they receive no future-need allocation.
allocation_detail: Met Council forecasts regional affordable-housing need and assigns shares to communities expecting sewer-serviced household growth. Plans must guide adequate land at qualifying densities, rather than guarantee production. Current 2021–2030 need and the 2031–2040 allocation for 2050 plans are distinct; the latter focuses on affordability at ≤30%, 31–50%, and 51–60% AMI.
enforcement: Local plans go to Met Council before final approval. Local zoning and controls must conform to the comprehensive plan; Met Council reviews plans against metropolitan planning requirements.
key_distinction: This is a metropolitan-region mandate with an affordable-need allocation, not a statewide requirement. Communities without forecast sewer-serviced growth still need a housing element but are exempt from allocation-dependent land requirements.

Stat. §473.121, subd.2: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.121 | Met Council, Allocation of Future Affordable Housing Need: https://metrocouncil.org/Housing/Planning/Affordable-Housing-Measures/Allocation-of-Affordable-Housing-NEED.aspx | Met Council, Imagine2050: Roles, responsibilities, and implementation: https://imagine2050.metrocouncil.org/reference-materials/housing/roles-responsibilities-and-implementation/ | Minn. contents: Housing needs (required): Existing and projected local/regional housing needs; 2050 guidance adds explicit analysis of existing community needs. | Income groups (required): Low/moderate income housing opportunities and the region's affordable-housing allocation. | Land capacity (conditional): Guide sufficient residential land at suitable density for allocated affordable need where sewer-serviced growth is forecast. | Action program (required): Housing implementation program using official controls, fiscal tools and sequenced actions. | Preservation (required): 2050 guidance includes maintenance/preservation and current housing needs within the implementation analysis.

name: South Carolina
housing_duty: Housing is a required comprehensive-plan element when a municipality undertakes the statutory comprehensive planning process.
plan_mandate: Creating a local planning commission is optional. A statutory comprehensive plan must include the housing element; housing-element adoption is also a prerequisite to land-development regulations under § 6-29-1130(A).
coverage: Municipalities/county planning jurisdictions using Chapter 29; no population cutoff. Plan elements may be adopted incrementally. Zoning requires at least land use; land-development regulations additionally require housing, community facilities, and priority investment elements.
assessment_detail: The local planning commission produces the surveys, inventory and statement of housing needs/goals for its planning jurisdiction. A municipality may use its own commission, a joint commission, or a county commission acting by agreement. Those local/joint arrangements assess need; the statute does not assign that assessment to a state agency.
assessment_method: Sections 6-29-340 and -510 prescribe the required process and subjects: conditions and probable future development, needs/goals, population and household trends, housing tenure/condition/affordability, and regulatory-cost/incentive analysis. The commission solicits housing-industry and finance input. The chapter prescribes no numerical state housing-need formula.
assessment_local_role: The responsible municipal, joint or county commission develops the analysis and recommends the element for adoption by the governing bodies. It considers adjacent jurisdictions and regional issues; no externally assigned municipal housing-unit share appears in this regime.
allocation_detail: The local commission inventories conditions and states needs/goals; it must consider regional conflicts. Chapter 29 does not assign quantified regional housing need to individual municipalities.
enforcement: Local hearings/adoption and periodic review apply. Housing-element adoption is required before land-development regulations; the reviewed chapter has no state municipal-need allocation or housing-element certification agency.
key_distinction: Housing is mandatory within the statutory plan, while state law does not compel every municipality to create that planning framework. Housing-stock inventory is not California’s developable-site inventory.
sources: S.C. Code §§ 6-29-320, -340, -510, -530, -720, -1130: https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t06c029.php
contents: Housing needs (required): Inventory existing housing location, type, age, condition, tenure and affordability; state needs and goals. This is housing-stock analysis, not a required parcel inventory. | Development constraints (required): Analyze unnecessary regulatory costs and market-based affordability incentives; solicit homebuilder, developer, contractor and housing-finance input. | Action program (required): Planning elements must have implementation strategies and time frames. | Monitoring (required): Review at least every five years and update the comprehensive plan including all elements at least every ten years.

name: Alabama
housing_duty: No express housing element or citywide housing-needs component appears in the reviewed master-plan contents.
plan_mandate: Municipalities may create a commission under § 11-52-2; an established commission has a master-plan duty under § 11-52-8.
coverage: General city/town planning framework statewide; no housing-specific population trigger in §§ 11-52-2 or -8.
assessment_detail: The municipal commission must study general present conditions and future growth, but the reviewed master-plan provisions do not specify a housing-need estimate or housing assessor.
assessment_method: Sections 11-52-8 and -9 identify physical-development topics and broad survey purposes, without a housing-unit demand formula or an incorporated state need estimate. The previously disclosed current official-code access gap remains.
assessment_local_role: An established commission performs general master planning and may include locally selected housing work. This review does not establish a required local housing calculation or an external assigned count.
allocation_detail: Section 11-52-8 enumerates physical-development and zoning recommendations without assigning housing need among municipalities. Section -9’s general attention to future growth is not municipal unit allocation.
enforcement: General master-plan adoption and public-project review procedures exist. The reviewed sections contain no housing-element certification or assigned housing-unit enforcement.
key_distinction: An Alabama city may include housing in its own plan. That local choice does not make the subject a state-required housing element.
uncertainties: The legislature’s current code app returned a shell instead of § 11-52-8 text. A current official statewide text check remains desirable; the 2025 mirror and City of Mobile reproduction agree on the operative contents.

name: Louisiana
housing_duty: The reviewed municipal master-plan statutes do not require a citywide housing element. General public-housing layout and blight replanning are permissible subjects.
plan_mandate: Municipalities may create a planning commission under § 33:102; the commission then shall prepare/adopt a master plan under § 33:106.
coverage: General statewide municipal regime plus the special Shreveport master-plan statute reviewed. No housing-specific population cutoff appears in those content provisions.
assessment_detail: Neither the general municipal master-plan provision nor the reviewed Shreveport provision requires a citywide housing-need estimate or designates a housing assessor.
assessment_method: Sections 33:106 and 33:140.8 prescribe general physical-planning recommendations; the optional public-housing/blight subjects contain no municipal housing-demand formula or state need total.
assessment_local_role: Municipal commissions prepare the general plan and may consider public-housing layout or blight. Those choices are not a required citywide housing-needs calculation, and no external housing-unit assignment appears in the reviewed provisions.
allocation_detail: Neither the general content statute nor the reviewed Shreveport provision identifies an external housing-need allocator or assigns municipal unit shares.
enforcement: No housing-element certification, housing production target, or housing-specific penalty appears in the reviewed master-plan provisions. General plan duties remain applicable to established commissions.
key_distinction: Public-housing layout is an optional physical-planning subject under § 33:106(B)(2); it does not require an inventory of all developable housing sites or a municipal needs assessment.

name: Kentucky
housing_duty: Housing is expressly optional as an additional element under § 100.187(6), and expressly encouraged by state housing policy in § 198A.025(9).
plan_mandate: The planning commission of each Chapter 100 planning unit must prepare a comprehensive plan.
coverage: Local planning commissions under Chapter 100 statewide; no population cutoff in the housing encouragement. The underlying plan duty attaches to established planning units.
assessment_detail: Housing is an optional local comprehensive-plan element. Section 198A.025 separately makes identifying Kentuckians’ basic housing needs a state policy objective, but these provisions do not establish a required municipal housing-need estimate or assign a state-calculated municipal number.
assessment_method: Section 100.187(6) leaves inclusion of the additional element to the planning commission. Section 198A.025 lists state policy objectives and encouragement, not a municipal housing-assessment formula or required local dataset.
assessment_local_role: A local commission may include a housing element and carry out housing analysis. The encouragement does not establish that it must do so or that any outside housing-unit estimate must be accommodated.
allocation_detail: The reviewed provisions encourage local housing planning without a municipal unit allocation. Section 198A.025 describes state housing-policy objectives, not an apportionment formula.
enforcement: Core comprehensive-plan requirements remain applicable, but these provisions establish no penalty for omitting the expressly optional housing element.
key_distinction: Kentucky is an explicit encouragement case. The state-owned-land inventory mentioned in § 198A.025 is a state policy objective, not a required municipal housing-site inventory.

name: Oregon
housing_duty: Goal 10 housing planning applies to all cities. Housing-capacity analyses and housing-production strategies impose expanded duties on designated jurisdictions.
plan_mandate: All cities must plan for housing through comprehensive plans complying with Statewide Planning Goal 10.
coverage: Basic duty: all cities. Expanded cycle generally applies at ≥10,000 population. ORS197A.015 also includes every Tillamook County city and Barview/Twin Rocks/Watseco, Cloverdale, Hebo, Neahkahnie, Neskowin, Netarts, Oceanside and Pacific City/Woods regardless of size, plus county jurisdiction over Metro urban unincorporated lands. Metro capacity cycle: six years; outside Metro: eight. Smaller cities also face inventory duties at specified plan reviews.
assessment_detail: The Oregon Department of Administrative Services conducts the annual Oregon Housing Needs Analysis, estimating statewide and regional needs over 20 years, underproduction, homelessness and second-home conversion. It allocates need to cities. Local housing-capacity and contextualized-needs analysis follows.
assessment_method: State statute identifies the components and income bands; DAS performs the analysis and considers population forecasts, regional job growth, equitable distribution and specified Metro projections. DLCD and Oregon Housing and Community Services assist DAS and may recommend methodological changes.
assessment_local_role: Cities use allocated need in their housing planning and assess buildable land, capacity and local context. Expanded jurisdictions prepare production strategies. Local capacity assessment is distinct from calculating the external 20-year need.
allocation_detail: DAS allocates 20-year need to each city and a separate Metro-unincorporated allocation to each Metro county. Need is segmented at <30%, 30–<60%, 60–<80%, 80–<120%, and ≥120% median family income. Separate six-/eight-year production targets apply to expanded-duty jurisdictions; these are distinct from the universal need allocation.
enforcement: DLCD reviews production strategies and may approve or remand them; its housing acceleration program tracks production and implementation for expanded jurisdictions.
key_distinction: The 10,000 cutoff is not an exemption from housing planning or from allocation of 20-year need. Distinguish statewide need allocation from the separate production-target/strategy system.

contents: Housing needs (required): Needed housing over the planning period; expanded-duty jurisdictions add contextualized needs. | Income groups (required): State allocations disaggregate affordability brackets. | Land / sites inventory (required): Goal 10 requires buildable residential land inventory. §197A.270 requires identifiable lots/parcels, except infill/redevelopment land; expanded program adds development-ready mapping. | Land capacity (required): Determine whether buildable land accommodates 20-year need; detailed cyclic analyses for expanded-duty jurisdictions. | Development constraints (conditional): Production strategies consider market conditions and development barriers. | Fair housing (conditional): Expanded production strategies must promote fair housing. | Action program (conditional): Expanded jurisdictions adopt timed housing-production actions, normally within a year after capacity-analysis deadline. | Monitoring (conditional): Mid-cycle production-strategy evaluation and state acceleration program for expanded jurisdictions.

name: Oklahoma
housing_duty: No express citywide housing element, housing-needs inventory, or housing allocation is required by the reviewed general and large-city plan-content provisions.
plan_mandate: General commissions are optional under § 45-101 and prepare plans under § 45-103. The additional large-city framework authorizes commissions with a master-plan duty under § 47-106.
coverage: General municipal commissions plus the separate large-city regime reviewed. Section 47-101 opens with a population threshold of at least 200,000 by latest federal census (its municipality definition says over 200,000); that is a planning-regime threshold, not a housing-element trigger.
assessment_detail: General municipal and regional commissions prepare development plans, and large-city commissions prepare master plans. The reviewed Title 11 provisions do not require a housing-need estimate or designate a housing assessor.
assessment_method: Sections 45-103, 46-103 and 47-106 provide survey/planning powers and physical-development subjects without a housing-demand formula or a state-calculated municipal planning total.
assessment_local_role: Commissions perform general physical planning and may investigate local development subjects. Regional cooperation or planning for residence is not, by itself, a required housing-needs assessment; the reviewed law supplies no external housing-unit share to accommodate.
allocation_detail: Neither municipal physical planning nor regional coordination in the reviewed Title 11 provisions apportions housing-unit need among municipalities.
enforcement: The reviewed provisions establish general planning duties; no dedicated housing-element certification or allocated-unit compliance requirement is identified.
key_distinction: Plans for a municipality’s betterment as a place of residence and a zoning plan do not themselves require a housing-needs element. Population thresholds distinguish commission powers, not housing obligations.
