name: Connecticut
housing_duty: New housing growth planning law effective January 1, 2026 replaces repealed §8-30j. First municipal/regional plans are due in 2028 or 2029, then every five years.
plan_mandate: Each municipality must prepare a housing growth plan or elect to comply with its regional plan. It may be combined with a coinciding plan of conservation and development.
coverage: All municipalities; no population cutoff. June 1, 2028: Capitol, Northeastern, Lower Connecticut River Valley, Northwest Hills and Southeastern regions. After June 1, 2028 but by June 1, 2029: South Central, Greater Bridgeport, Naugatuck Valley and Western regions. The lowest twenty municipalities by adjusted equalized net grand list per capita have preservation-focused plans and are excluded from recommended-goal allocation.
assessment_detail: Under the enacted framework, OPM's Secretary evaluates ten-year housing need and determines statewide and regional housing-growth targets. COGs then produce regional assessments recommending municipal affordable-unit goals. First state targets are due December 1, 2026, so completed implementation is not presumed.
assessment_method: Section 8-13dd(b) sets state evaluation factors including replacement, affordability, household formation, demographics and cost burden. Section (c) governs COG methods for municipal recommendations, subject to OPM review, fair-housing factors and the recommendation ceiling.
assessment_local_role: A municipality writes its growth plan or elects the regional plan. A municipality writing its own plan adopts an affordable goal and may depart from the COG recommendation with written reasons. Its site/infrastructure analysis is separate from OPM's state/regional need determination.
allocation_authority: COGs recommend municipal goals; OPM approves
allocation_detail: Enacted framework, first targets pending: OPM sets state/regional growth targets by December 1, 2026; COGs recommend municipal affordable-unit shares by June 1, 2027, with OPM approval. Recommended goals are capped at 20% of occupied units. A municipality preparing its own plan may adopt a different goal with written reasons; this is an advisory allocation, not California-style binding need.
enforcement: COG review, OPM approval limited to statutory conformity, and annual reporting. Late plans affect access to new §8-30g moratoria; growth-program awards depend on progress.
key_distinction: Legally enacted now, but initial plans and recommended shares are not yet due. Municipalities can explain departures from the recommended regional goal.
timing_note: First targets pending; municipal plans due in 2028 or 2029.
uncertainties: OPM's implementation guidelines and first targets were not independently located in this review. Classification concerns the statutory framework, not completed implementation.

contents: Land / sites inventory (required): Inventory developable land; identify practicable zones/parcels and maximum density for the affordable goal. | Land capacity (required): Identify infrastructure needs, including wastewater capacity. | Fair housing (required): Explain compliance with fair housing, choice and economic-diversity duties. | Action program (required): Housing diversity, disability accessibility, consistency with other plans, and implementation schedule. | Monitoring (required): Annual progress reports after plan approval. | Preservation (conditional): Lowest twenty wealth-measure municipalities prioritize existing affordability, rehabilitation, displacement prevention and infrastructure.

name: Utah
housing_duty: Specified municipalities must include a moderate-income housing element meeting §10-21-201. Other municipalities are encouraged to address moderate-income housing.
plan_mandate: Each municipality must prepare and adopt a comprehensive, long-range general plan under §10-20-401.
coverage: Cities of the first through fourth classes (population at least 10,000), plus fifth-class cities with population at least 5,000 in first-, second- or third-class counties (county population at least 40,000). A municipality newly qualifying as of January 1 must amend its plan by August 1 that year. Fixed-guideway public-transit stations trigger additional strategy requirements.
assessment_detail: The municipal planning commission drafts the moderate-income housing element and analyzes the locality’s realistic opportunity to meet additional moderate-income housing needs over the next five years. The identified duty is local planning, not receipt of a state-calculated municipal housing-need number.
assessment_method: State law sets the five-year horizon, moderate-income focus, strategy menu and implementation/reporting requirements. The reviewed§10-21-201 does not prescribe a state formula assigning each municipality a unit total. State compliance review examines the resulting plan and implementation.
assessment_local_role: The planning commission analyzes local opportunities and selects the required strategy combination; the municipality adopts and implements its plan. No external regional unit allocation was identified in the reviewed provisions.
allocation_detail: The municipality analyzes how it will give a realistic opportunity to meet additional moderate-income housing needs during the next five years. The reviewed provisions prescribe strategy menus and implementation duties, not an externally allocated regional unit share.
enforcement: State review determines compliance and allows cure and appeal. Noncompliance can cause specified transportation-funding ineligibility and daily fees; the statute also authorizes injunctive enforcement. The 2026 reporting pause preserves qualifying 2025 compliance; normal implementation reporting resumes in 2027.
key_distinction: This is a mandatory planning-and-strategy system for a population-defined subset, not a California-style assigned unit obligation. The 2025 recodification and July 2026 amendments make older §10-9a citations and older strategy counts incomplete.

contents: Housing needs (required): Analyze the municipality's additional moderate-income housing needs for the next five years and realistic opportunities to meet them. | Income groups (required): The element focuses on moderate-income housing, defined as affordable at 80% of county median gross household income, adjusted for household size. | Action program (required): Without a fixed-guideway station: select at least three listed strategies, or at least one of the special housing-zone/density-bonus strategies (X)–(CC). With a station: five including station-area planning and specified transit-density or parking reform, or the alternative three-strategy combination. Adopt a five-year implementation timeline with specific benchmarks. | Monitoring (required): Specified municipalities report implementation actions and barriers, ADUs, entitlements, building permits, occupancy and zoning information. The ordinary report is due August 1; 2026 has a statutory reporting pause and carryover compliance, with a separate July 1 occupancy-count requirement. | Development constraints (conditional): Strategies can address zoning, fees, parking, infrastructure and approvals; no single reform is universally required because municipalities choose among statutory alternatives.

name: Nevada
housing_duty: A housing element is mandatory for cities and counties in counties with at least 100,000 people. Below that county threshold it is an optional listed master-plan element.
plan_mandate: Planning commissions prepare and adopt a long-range master plan. City and county governing bodies may adopt all or portions, subject to mandatory elements; in counties of at least 700,000 the governing body must adopt the complete listed master plan.
coverage: The trigger is county population, not city population: counties with 100,000–699,999 must retain housing even in a partial plan; counties of at least 700,000 must adopt all listed elements. The housing element is optional below 100,000.
assessment_detail: The local planning commission and city/county governing body analyze housing conditions, projected growth and present/prospective attainable-housing needs.
assessment_method: Section 278.160 specifies inventories and analyses. Housing Division reporting forms and compilation of reports provide oversight, not a state formula calculating the controlling local housing need.
assessment_local_role: Localities prepare their needs analysis, available-parcel inventory and five-year attainable-housing strategy, then implement required measures and report results.
allocation_detail: The local master-plan housing element determines present and prospective needs and suitable housing land. The reviewed master-plan and regional-planning provisions do not assign each city a state-calculated fair share. State compilation of local reports does not constitute municipal allocation.
enforcement: Covered governing bodies must adopt at least six statutory housing measures and submit annual reports to the Housing Division; § 278.237 also requires annual reporting to the Division and the Advisory Committee on Housing. These are planning, implementation and reporting duties, not a guarantee that a specified number of homes will be built.
key_distinction: County population controls city coverage. The 2025 revised code uses attainable housing and requires at least six implementation measures; neither creates a California-style municipal allocation.

Stat. §§ 278.235, 278.237: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/nrs/nrs-278.html#NRS278Sec235 | Nev. Rev. Stat. §§ 278.02528, 278.0272, 278.0274: https://www.leg.state.nv.us/nrs/nrs-278.html#NRS278Sec0274
contents: Housing needs (required): Analyze housing conditions, existing stock, projected demographic growth and present/prospective attainable-housing needs. | Income groups (required): Plan adequate housing regardless of income and inventory attainable rental/ownership housing, subsidies and disability-accessible housing. Current code uses defined attainable-housing categories. | Land / sites inventory (required): Inventory available parcels suitable for residential development, including zoning, environmental and other restrictions. This is an actual sites inventory. | Land capacity (required): Inventory land characteristics suitable for housing and infrastructure sufficient for current and projected growth. | Development constraints (required): Identify and plan to mitigate impediments to attainable housing. | Preservation (required): Analyze methods addressing need through new construction, conversion and rehabilitation; maintain and develop attainable housing. | Action program (required): Prepare an attainable-housing plan for at least five years and adopt at least six of the measures listed in § 278.235. | Monitoring (required): Annual March 15 report on implementation measures/results and need; July 15 report on housing-element contents and five-year attainable/market-rate housing plans. State agencies compile/publicize reports.

name: Iowa
housing_duty: The housing information in §18B.2(2)(d) is expressly optional: municipalities may include plans for adequate housing supply, housing-stock analysis, and policies for diverse choices and rehabilitation. Required consideration of smart-planning principles is not a required housing element.
plan_mandate: City zoning regulations must accord with a comprehensive plan. A zoning commission may recommend, and the city council may adopt, a comprehensive plan; §414.3 does not direct every city to adopt a separate plan. Plans and land-development regulations must consider the smart-planning principles.
coverage: The smart-planning chapter defines municipality as a city or county. No population cutoff appears in its optional housing guidelines. The Iowa Jobs II disaster-prevention grant statute separately conditions eligibility on applying the smart-planning principles and guidelines, but does not expressly convert every optional housing topic into mandatory plan content.
assessment_detail: The optional housing guideline names existing and forecast housing demand but establishes neither a mandatory municipal need estimate nor a designated state or regional assessor.
assessment_method: State law identifies optional topics and examples of stock characteristics; it does not prescribe a housing-demand forecasting formula in these sections.
assessment_local_role: A city or county can choose to analyze housing stock and future demand and incorporate policies in its plan or land-development regulations. No external municipal number is identified.
allocation_detail: The reviewed smart-planning and municipal zoning provisions do not assign a state or regional housing-unit share to cities. Existing and forecast housing demand is an optional local planning topic.
enforcement: §414.3 provides council adoption, published notice and distribution of an adopted comprehensive plan. The reviewed provisions contain no housing-element certification or penalty for omitting the optional housing material. §16.194A has a separate smart-planning condition for disaster-prevention grants.
key_distinction: “Shall consider” smart-planning principles coexists with “may include” housing content. HF2618 proposed to eliminate the chapter in 2026, but its official history shows House passage only, not enactment.
sources: Iowa Code §§18B.1(6), 18B.2(1)(c), (2)(d), (m) (2026): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/2026/18B.pdf | Iowa Code §414.3 (2026): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/2026/414.3.pdf | Iowa Code §16.194A(2) (2026): https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/code/2026/16.194A.pdf | Iowa Legislature, HF2618 bill history, 91st General Assembly: https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislation/billTracking/billHistory?billName=HF2618&ga=91
contents: Housing needs (encouraged): Plans to ensure adequate supply for existing and forecast housing demand are optional. | Other content (encouraged): Optional inventory and analysis concerns existing housing stock—age, condition, type, market value, occupancy, and history—not a parcel inventory of developable sites. | Preservation (encouraged): Optional policies can support maintenance and rehabilitation of existing housing. | Action program (encouraged): Optional policies and programs can promote new housing and a range of housing choices; implementation actions may be compiled in the plan.

name: Arkansas
housing_duty: No express housing element, required housing-needs estimate or standing equivalent municipal housing-policy plan was identified in the reviewed municipal planning provisions. They authorize land-use, community-facilities, master-street and other plans with general development objectives.
plan_mandate: Cities of the first and second class and incorporated towns have power to adopt and enforce municipal plans. The framework is elective; if used, a land-use plan precedes a recommended zoning ordinance, and prescribed studies/adoption procedures apply.
coverage: Reviewed the municipal framework for first-class cities, second-class cities and incorporated towns, including actual plan-content provisions. No housing-element population trigger was identified. The former extraterritorial planning thresholds were repealed by 2025 Act 314 and are not housing-element cutoffs.
assessment_detail: The planning commission must undertake suitable studies for the plans it prepares, but the listed plan subjects do not require a quantified housing-needs assessment or designate a housing-demand assessor.
assessment_method: §14-56-414(a) requires suitable plan-related studies and specifies their sequence. Neither that section’s land-use/facilities/street topics nor §14-56-403’s general objectives prescribe a housing-demand formula in the reviewed text.
assessment_local_role: The city and its commission choose plans and perform relevant studies under the statutory process. A voluntarily prepared local housing study is not coded as a mandated municipal assessment.
allocation_detail: The reviewed municipal planning provisions do not specify a state/regional housing-needs total or assign municipal housing-unit shares. Required suitable studies of a chosen plan do not establish external need allocation.
enforcement: The planning framework uses a commission hearing, certification to the city legislative body, local adoption and filing. The 2025 administrative-rezoning pathway has a limited exception. No state housing-element approval or housing-need target sanction is identified in the reviewed provisions.
key_distinction: The 2025 ADU law directly preempts specified local restrictions; it does not establish a housing element or an external need allocation. General authority to prepare plans and suitable studies is not an express housing assessment mandate.
uncertainties: Core §§14-56-402, 403 and 414 were read in the 2025 code reproduction and checked against Municipal League guidance, but the state-linked official Lexis consolidated text did not expose readable sections. Official 2025 Acts 313, 314 and 595 were read; full current consolidated primary-code verification remains.

name: Kansas
housing_duty: No express housing element or standing equivalent municipal housing-policy plan was identified in the reviewed general planning statutes. Required plan surveys and residential land-use recommendations are broader than a housing-needs element. A separate community needs analysis is required before voluntarily creating a Reinvestment Housing Incentive District.
plan_mandate: A city may create a planning commission, which is authorized to prepare and adopt a comprehensive plan subject to governing-body approval. §12-747 prescribes surveys, recommendations, hearings and annual review when a plan is prepared; it does not require every city to adopt one.
coverage: The general municipal planning framework applies without a housing-specific population cutoff. The separate district program is open to city or county governing bodies; it concerns selected housing-development districts, not a statewide general-plan housing requirement.
assessment_detail: §12-747 does not expressly require a housing-demand estimate or designate a housing-need assessor. Separately, §12-5244 does require the city/county governing body to conduct a community housing-needs analysis before creating an incentive district, with state concurrence in its findings; that project-financing pathway is outside the general-plan classification.
assessment_method: General-plan surveys cover land use, population/building intensity, facilities, transport, economic conditions and natural resources. For the separate incentive-district analysis, state law requires findings about quality housing shortages across price ranges, persistence, economic effects and need for incentives; the locality conducts the analysis and the Secretary reviews those findings.
assessment_local_role: The local commission prepares general-plan surveys and recommendations. A locality electing an incentive district separately analyzes its community’s housing needs and adopts a district development/feasibility plan after state concurrence; it receives no externally apportioned unit obligation.
allocation_detail: No external municipal housing-need allocation is specified in the general planning framework. In the separate district financing program, the Secretary of Commerce reviews the locality’s shortage findings but does not assign a municipal share of statewide or regional need.
enforcement: For a comprehensive plan, §12-747 requires a hearing, governing-body approval, publication and at least annual commission review. No housing-element certification or omission penalty is identified there. The separate incentive-district program requires Secretary of Commerce concurrence in shortage findings before proceeding and a local development plan/hearing.
key_distinction: The general-plan finding is scoped: Kansas does require an actual local community housing-needs analysis for voluntary incentive districts. State review of that analysis is not state assessment or fair-share allocation, and the district project plan is not treated as a standing municipal housing element.

name: Mississippi
housing_duty: Housing must be included in the community-facilities plan that forms a basis for a capital-improvements program. The comprehensive plan also requires long-range residential-development goals and a residential land-use distribution/density description. This is a narrow required housing topic, not a separately specified housing-needs element.
plan_mandate: Municipal zoning authority is discretionary; zoning regulations must accord with a comprehensive plan. When adopted, the statutory comprehensive plan must contain the minimum components defined in §17-1-1(c). The reviewed provisions do not direct every municipality to adopt a plan independently of that framework.
coverage: The comprehensive-plan definition covers the entire municipality or county; municipality includes any incorporated city, town or village. No population cutoff appears. Coverage is conditional on the comprehensive-planning/zoning framework rather than a universal municipal housing-plan adoption command.
assessment_detail: The statutory minimum housing topic does not require a quantified housing-demand estimate or identify a state, regional or local institution that must produce one. Population and economic-growth projections may inform quantitative land-use recommendations, but are not a mandatory housing-needs calculation.
assessment_method: §17-1-1(c) identifies planning topics and permits demographic/economic projections as a basis for land-use recommendations; no housing-needs formula or required forecasting methodology is specified there.
assessment_local_role: The local governing body adopts the comprehensive plan and its community-facilities/housing topic. The reviewed minimum-content provisions assign no external unit number to be accommodated.
allocation_detail: No state or regional housing-unit apportionment to municipalities is specified in the reviewed minimum-plan and zoning-conformity provisions. Optional use of population/economic projections to inform land-use recommendations is not an assigned municipal housing share.
enforcement: The identified statutory connection is that zoning regulations must be made in accordance with a comprehensive plan. The reviewed minimum-content provisions do not establish state housing-element certification, a housing-specific periodic update, or a sanction for missing a housing-unit target.
key_distinction: An express housing topic exists even though the statute lacks the detailed housing-element machinery found elsewhere. A required community-facilities item does not by itself mandate a needs forecast, sites inventory or fair-share allocation.
uncertainties: The core housing text was verified in the official enacted 2018 act and corroborated against the 2025 code reproduction, but the current official consolidated publisher text was not accessible. The §17-1-9 conformity provision was read in the 2025 reproduction; a final official consolidation check remains.

contents: Other content (required): Housing is an express item in the community-facilities plan; long-range goals must address residential development and the land-use plan must describe residential distribution and densities. Generic land-use mapping is not treated as a parcel inventory of housing sites. | Action program (required): The community-facilities plan, including housing, is to serve as a basis for a capital-improvements program. No housing-specific action schedule or production quota is stated.

name: New Mexico
housing_duty: An adopted affordable-housing plan, reviewed by Housing New Mexico/Mortgage Finance Authority (MFA), is a prerequisite for local Affordable Housing Act donations. Rule 4.1 specifies community-wide needs, land-use analysis and goals, subject to feasibility and readily available data.
plan_mandate: A county or municipality using the Affordable Housing Act to make housing-assistance grants/donations must have an existing valid affordable-housing plan or housing elements within its general plan. This is a standing community housing strategy, which may be separate from the comprehensive plan.
coverage: Counties and municipalities making housing-assistance grants under the Affordable Housing Act, with no population cutoff. Grants include land, buildings and housing/infrastructure costs; participation is the trigger. The municipal definition includes incorporated cities, towns and villages and specified incorporated/H-class counties.
assessment_detail: The participating county or municipality prepares a housing-needs assessment, either individually or through an optional joint county/municipal plan addressing each entity’s needs.
assessment_method: MFA Rule 4.1 requires demographic/market analysis, cost-burden/overcrowding/special-needs measures, AMI affordability gaps and projected units by tenure, type and cost. Required elements are qualified by feasibility and readily available data; no state-apportioned unit formula is specified.
assessment_local_role: The local governing body adopts the plan and housing ordinance. A joint plan must disaggregate data and recommendations. MFA reviews compliance; locality/joint planners generate the needs estimates and quantified objectives.
allocation_authority: No external allocator identified; MFA reviews compliance
allocation_detail: Local governments prepare their own estimates of existing and projected need and unit objectives; they may jointly plan with needs disaggregated for each participant. MFA approves plan/ordinance compliance but does not assign an external municipal fair-share number under the reviewed Act and rules.
enforcement: MFA reviews plans and enabling ordinances; the local governing body must adopt/pass them. Proposed ordinances must be submitted at least 45 days before enactment under § 6-27-7. Rule 4.2 makes failure to submit required documents or comply with an invalidity determination invalidate the ordinance and acts under it. These controls condition donations, not universal local housing production.
key_distinction: The law requires a standing adopted community housing plan as a donation prerequisite, not merely a project financing plan. State approval of locally produced need estimates is different from state allocation.

Rule 4.1 applies when feasible and data are readily available. | Income groups (conditional): Identify housing-cost/income gaps by AMI and unit objectives by income levels, subject to the Rule 4.1 feasibility/data qualifier. | Land / sites inventory (conditional): Analyze land-use parcels by zoning, size, use, environmental constraints and infrastructure; evaluate suitability and availability of developable sites. This is site analysis, not an expressly prescribed parcel-table format; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier. | Land capacity (conditional): Evaluate realistic development capacity of developable sites, appropriate special-needs housing zoning and minimum affordable-housing density calculations; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier. | Development constraints (conditional): Identify regulatory, permit, fee, infrastructure, financing, land-price, construction-cost and local administrative constraints; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier. | Fair housing (conditional): Identify programs/agencies promoting access and equal opportunity to affordable housing, including assistance for people with disabilities; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier. | Preservation (conditional): Determine homes to be created through construction, rehabilitation and preservation, with quantifiable objectives; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier. | Action program (conditional): Quantifiable time-period objectives, responsible programs/agencies, incentives to remove constraints and potential financing sources; subject to Rule 4.1 qualifier.

name: Idaho
housing_duty: Housing is a listed mandatory comprehensive-plan component, subject to the express exception allowing the plan to explain why a particular component is unneeded.
plan_mandate: Every city and county must exercise the Local Land Use Planning Act powers. The planning commission, or governing board exercising its powers, prepares, implements, reviews and updates a comprehensive plan.
coverage: All cities and counties; no population threshold. Section 67-6508 permits omission of a component when the plan specifies why it is unneeded. County jurisdiction is over unincorporated territory.
assessment_detail: The city or county planning commission, or governing board acting in its place, conducts the housing-conditions and needs analysis.
assessment_method: State law specifies subjects, including population trends and housing conditions, but the reviewed sections prescribe no statewide housing-unit formula.
assessment_local_role: The locality prepares and adopts the analysis and housing provisions; it may explain why a component is unneeded. No externally assigned housing number was identified.
allocation_detail: The local planning body analyzes housing conditions and community needs. No state or regional assignment of a quantified municipal share was identified in the reviewed Local Land Use Planning Act provisions.
enforcement: Plans and amendments require commission hearing procedures and governing-board adoption by resolution. The reviewed sections establish local planning duties and adoption procedures, without an identified state housing-element certification or assigned-unit enforcement process.
key_distinction: Housing is presumptively required statewide, but a locality may expressly justify omitting a component as unneeded; this is not an unconditional housing-element mandate.

contents: Housing needs (conditional): Analyze housing conditions and needs, alongside population trends. This component is subject to the statutory unneeded-component exception. | Income groups (conditional): Provide for low-cost conventional housing; this is not an express allocation across numerical income bands. Subject to the component exception. | Action program (conditional): Plan improvements to housing standards and safe, sanitary, adequate housing, including manufactured/mobile-home siting sufficient to maintain competitive markets. General implementation component covers actions, programs, budgets, ordinances and expenditure schedules. | Other content (conditional): General land-use analysis maps suitable projected uses, including housing. It is not an express inventory of available housing parcels.

name: Nebraska
housing_duty: Covered cities must adopt an affordable housing action plan and submit biennial affordable-housing reports. The action-plan deadline was January 1, 2023 for cities of at least 50,000 and January 1, 2024 for smaller covered cities.
plan_mandate: The Municipal Density and Missing Middle Housing Act requires covered cities to adopt an affordable housing action plan, either within the comprehensive plan or as a separate plan. Thus its housing duty does not depend on an optional decision to adopt a general plan.
coverage: “City” means a metropolitan-class city, primary-class city, or first-class city with at least 20,000 inhabitants, determined by the most recent federal decennial census or revised certified Census Bureau count. The under-50,000 deadline does not extend the act to every small municipality.
assessment_detail: Each covered city must report a demographic analysis with trends and estimated housing need by housing type and price range. This is a city-produced estimate accompanying the affordable housing action-plan regime.
assessment_method: State law prescribes demographic trends and type/price-range categories for the estimate, but these provisions provide no statewide forecasting or municipal-share formula. The affordable-housing definition references HUD income limits as they existed January 1, 2022; that definition does not make HUD or the state the need assessor.
assessment_local_role: The city prepares the need analysis, adopts numerical construction and zoning goals, selects incentives and zoning updates, and reports to the Legislature’s Urban Affairs Committee.
allocation_detail: Each covered city estimates housing need and sets its own construction and zoning goals. No state/regional housing need apportioned among cities appears in §§19-5503–5505; the legislative committee receives reports rather than assigning unit shares.
enforcement: Cities must transmit adopted plans and biennial reports to the Urban Affairs Committee, which may require a public presentation. Failure to adopt the required action plan triggers a duty to permit middle housing in residential areas allowing detached single-family dwellings and a duplex on every such lot, with conforming ordinance changes.
key_distinction: The statutory definition limits the apparent “each city” duty. Locally chosen unit and zoning goals are not externally allocated need. The 2026 LB839 reporting amendment was vetoed and its override failed.

contents: Housing needs (required): Biennial report must include demographic trends and estimates of housing need classified by housing type and price range. | Income groups (required): The action plan addresses affordable, middle and workforce housing. Affordable housing is defined using the statutory 80-percent income-limit standard; report estimates are classified by price range. | Other content (required): Construction goals must identify types, numbers and geographic locations of new units; this is not an express parcel-by-parcel developable-site inventory. | Action program (required): Plan must include actions to encourage construction, goals for the percentage of residential areas allowing multifamily/middle housing, incentive plans, and zoning updates. | Monitoring (required): Biennial July 1 reports beginning 2021 cover zoning, construction and annexation over the prior five years, costs, incentives, blighted areas and action-plan progress.

name: West Virginia
housing_duty: Every Chapter 8A comprehensive plan must include a housing component with goals, plans and programs for current and anticipated residents. This is mandatory plan content within an elective planning/zoning framework, not a universal command for every municipality to adopt a plan.
plan_mandate: A municipality may create a planning commission. Once established, the commission must prepare and recommend a comprehensive plan; a municipality exercising Chapter 8A zoning authority adopts a comprehensive plan. Joint/regional planning is available with municipal consent.
coverage: No population cutoff in the housing-content requirement. It applies throughout the planning commission’s jurisdiction; county, multicounty, regional or joint plans count as a municipality’s plan only with the required municipal consent. A special joint airport-hazard plan under §8A-3-3(f) can exist without a full comprehensive plan.
assessment_detail: The planning commission preparing the comprehensive plan conducts surveys and studies and analyzes projected housing needs, types and necessary units. The commission may be municipal, county, multicounty, regional or joint; a nonmunicipal plan requires municipal consent to count as the municipal plan.
assessment_method: §8A-3-2 requires surveys and studies of existing conditions/services and probable future changes; §8A-3-4 requires projected housing need and unit numbers. These sections prescribe analysis topics, not a uniform state-produced estimate or mathematical allocation formula.
assessment_local_role: The municipality can prepare through its own commission or consent to a county/joint/regional plan. Its governing body adopts the plan, and the preparing commission identifies projected need and sufficient land.
allocation_detail: The preparing local or joint/regional commission projects necessary housing units and sufficient land for its jurisdiction. Chapter 8A does not identify a state or regional total assigned as municipal fair shares; a jointly prepared plan is not by itself an external allocation.
enforcement: The planning commission recommends the plan to the governing body; plan adoption is part of the statutory zoning pathway. After adoption the commission must follow, review and update the plan at least every ten years. The reviewed provisions contain no state housing-element certification or externally assigned unit-production sanction.
key_distinction: West Virginia expressly requires both a housing chapter and projected housing units in a plan, but leaves assessment with the preparing local/joint/regional commission. Optional creation of a commission does not make its housing content optional.

contents: Housing needs (required): Analyze projected needs and housing types for current and anticipated residents, including the number of necessary units. | Income groups (required): Housing analysis expressly includes affordable housing; the section does not prescribe income-band quotas. | Land capacity (required): Identify sufficient land needed for all housing needs alongside projected necessary units. The statute does not specify a parcel-level inventory or detailed zoning-capacity methodology. | Preservation (required): Address substandard housing, rehabilitation/improvement of existing housing, and adaptive reuse of buildings. | Other content (required): Analyze universally designed housing accessible to persons with disabilities. | Action program (required): Housing goals, plans and programs sit within a plan with timelines, implementation strategies and financing recommendations. | Monitoring (required): After adoption the commission must follow the plan, review it and make updates at least every ten years.

name: Hawaii
housing_duty: The reviewed state county-planning provisions do not expressly prescribe a separate housing element or a specified housing-needs/site-inventory package. They do require attention to applicable state policies, which include affordable housing objectives; county charters and plans can impose additional housing content.
plan_mandate: County zoning must operate within a long-range comprehensive general plan. County general/development plans state population and physical-development patterns, address local needs, further applicable State Planning Act provisions and consider state functional plans.
coverage: The relevant local planning units are counties, including the City and County of Honolulu. The state provisions apply to county planning rather than creating a population-triggered duty for independent cities. Section 46-4 excludes specified forest-reserve lands from its zoning framework.
assessment_detail: Sections 46-4 and 226-58 require sound county planning and consideration of state policy, but specify no controlling general-plan housing-demand calculation or assessor. State housing research and functional planning are separate from that scoped finding.
assessment_method: County plans use sound rationale, data, analyses and public/agency input. State functional plans are prepared by the responsible state agency with county participation, but the cited law supplies no municipal housing-share formula.
assessment_local_role: Counties formulate their plans under their charters, address local needs and consider statewide functional plans. No externally assigned housing-unit number was identified as controlling their general plans.
allocation_detail: No mandatory state/regional allocation of housing need to county general plans was identified in the reviewed provisions. State functional housing planning and published county housing-demand estimates do not, without an operative adoption/allocation duty, establish such an assignment.
enforcement: Section 46-4 requires zoning within the comprehensive-plan framework and provides county zoning enforcement/appeals; § 226-58 directs county plan formulation and consideration of state functional plans. The reviewed provisions contain no separate housing-element certification or assigned-housing-number enforcement process.
key_distinction: Hawaiʻi has state housing objectives and state functional planning, while local planning is county-based. Those features should not be counted automatically as a state-mandated housing element or municipal housing allocation.

name: New Hampshire
housing_duty: RSA 674:2 III(l) authorizes a housing section but does not require municipalities to include it. RPCs nevertheless must produce regional housing needs assessments; zoning municipalities separately must provide reasonable and realistic workforce-housing opportunities.
plan_mandate: Established planning boards must prepare and update master plans. Adopting zoning requires the mandatory vision and land-use sections; housing is expressly an optional section.
coverage: Optional housing section available statewide, without a population trigger. The separate workforce-housing obligation applies to every municipality exercising land-use ordinance/regulation powers.
assessment_detail: Each regional planning commission must assess housing need for persons and families at all income levels at least every five years. An optional local housing section assesses local conditions and projects needs in the municipality and region with reference to that RPC assessment.
assessment_method: RSA 36:47 specifies regional scope, all incomes and five-year updates, not a mandatory numerical fair-share formula. RPCs use a shared Fair Share Housing Production Model, supported by state demographic inputs, that combines household growth, employment and vacancy adjustments; using the fair-share model is optional.
assessment_local_role: Municipalities may use and refine regional model estimates when writing their optional housing chapter. A zoning municipality must meet the separate workforce-housing opportunity duty and can defend compliance based on existing stock sufficient for its fair share; no automatically binding model number is imposed.
allocation_authority: Regional planning commissions publish optional fair-share model results
allocation_detail: RPC fair-share modeling produces municipal production estimates by tenure/income, but RPC authority is advisory and the published model expressly says fair-share analyses are not required. RSA 674:59 creates an enforceable reasonable-opportunity duty, not a legislated unit allocation or mandatory fair-share formula.
enforcement: There is no housing-chapter adoption mandate to enforce. Workforce-housing applicants may separately appeal denials or economically damaging conditions under RSA 674:61; courts may permit development. A municipal claim that existing stock meets its fair share can be challenged.
key_distinction: Mandatory regional needs assessment and enforceable workforce-housing zoning duties coexist with an optional municipal housing chapter and advisory fair-share model.

name: Maine
housing_duty: Covered comprehensive plans must address housing supply, affordability and projected needs. The operative review rule contains a housing section. A 2025 rewrite of the growth-management statute has a protected transition for plan submissions, rather than immediately replacing every plan’s existing requirements.
plan_mandate: Growth-management planning is generally authorized rather than universal. Municipalities exercising ordinary zoning powers must have a consistent adopted comprehensive plan, subject to statutory exceptions; voluntary growth-management plans also must satisfy the planning requirements.
coverage: Municipalities and multimunicipal regions undertaking growth-management planning, particularly those using zoning powers. No housing-plan population cutoff. The zoning statute exempts an adult-entertainment-only ordinance; shoreland/floodplain exceptions appear in § 4314. Separate housing-data reporting at population 4,000 is not the housing-element coverage rule.
assessment_detail: The municipality or multimunicipal region prepares its comprehensive-plan housing forecast, using MaineHousing and state planning data. Separately, DECD and MaineHousing established statewide and county production goals; those do not replace the locally prepared planning assessment or assign a municipal share.
assessment_method: The state review rule specifies questions on added units, tenure, income, demographics, seasonal conversions and regulatory barriers. MaineHousing supplies data. The 2025 rewrite retains local or multimunicipal needs assessment and state rulemaking, with a transition. The separate state/county goals use a state-commissioned housing-needs study.
assessment_local_role: The local or joint planning body estimates additional units and affordability needs, decides which needs can be addressed locally or regionally, and proposes policies. It must also design ordinances to further fair-housing purposes in pursuit of state/regional production goals; no municipal need allocation is specified.
allocation_authority: No municipal need allocator; state rule supplies an affordability benchmark
allocation_detail: No state/regional assignment of a municipal unit need was identified. State production goals are set at statewide and county scales; the report expressly says meeting or exceeding them is not mandatory. The comprehensive-plan review rule asks communities to seek at least 10% of new residential development over the next decade as affordable: a percentage benchmark, not an allocated share of regional demand.
enforcement: The Maine Office of Community Affairs reviews submitted plans for completeness and consistency and identifies deficiencies affecting zoning, growth-rate and impact-fee ordinances. Zoning must be consistent with the comprehensive plan. State certification and planning assistance are distinct from a guarantee of housing production.
key_distinction: The state’s county goals and state-provided data are separate from the locally or jointly prepared plan forecast. The rule’s 10% affordability benchmark is not municipal allocation of need.
timing_note: 2025 statutory rewrite has a rule-dependent transition; existing review criteria remain relevant to protected submissions.
uncertainties: No final adoption date for rules implementing P.L. 2025 ch. 393 was located. The record preserves the § 53 transition and currently published review rule; it does not assume every submission uses the rewritten statute.

name: Montana
housing_duty: Covered Land Use Planning Act jurisdictions must quantify housing needs, inventory available sites and provide regulations allowing the needed housing. Optional chapter 1 growth policies also list existing and projected housing needs.
plan_mandate: The Montana Land Use Planning Act requires covered municipalities to adopt a land-use plan and future land-use map. Other local governments may opt into that Act. Outside it, adopted growth policies under chapter 1 must address listed subjects, including housing needs, with statutory discretion over detail.
coverage: Mandatory chapter 25 coverage: municipality population at least 5,000 within a county population at least 70,000, both under the most recent decennial census. Other local governments may opt in by affirmative vote and later opt out. Chapter 25 compliance exempts the jurisdiction from Title 76 chapters 1, 2, 3 and 8.
assessment_detail: The local governing body identifies and quantifies existing and projected needed housing types over the 20-year planning horizon.
assessment_method: State law specifies analytical subjects and demographic inputs: Census data plus permanent/seasonal population projections from Commerce, the local government or a specialist firm. If projections are unavailable, use proportional county population/growth. This population rule is not a state housing-need assessment.
assessment_local_role: Localities quantify need, may incorporate adopted housing assessments, and identify sites and regulations. Where documented constraints prevent meeting total need, they establish a feasible minimum number and actions to remove constraints.
allocation_detail: The local governing body estimates its own housing needs for projected population. State demographic projections are one permitted input, and a county-share population fallback exists, but no state/regional municipal housing-unit allocation is prescribed in the reviewed provisions.
enforcement: Chapter 25 requires regulations accommodating locally identified housing, implementation schedules and five-year progress documentation. The plan itself is not a regulatory document. The quantified need is a local planning obligation, with a documented-constraints provision, rather than an externally assigned construction quota. In March 2026, the Montana Supreme Court reversed the ruling that the Act facially violated public-participation rights.
key_distinction: The newer urban Act imposes a genuine sites inventory and quantified housing duty; its 5,000-city AND 70,000-county test and transition exceptions must be read together. State population inputs do not make this a state allocation regime.
timing_note: For municipalities qualifying on May 17, 2023, ordinary compliance deadline was May 17, 2026. A growth policy adopted within the preceding five years permits the later of that deadline or five years after policy adoption. Newly qualifying census municipalities comply by December 31 of the third year after that census; voluntary participants by December 31 of the fifth year after their vote.

contents: Housing needs (required): Quantify existing/projected needed housing types, location, age, condition and occupancy for the projected population over 20 years. | Land / sites inventory (required): Inventory available zoned, unzoned, vacant, underutilized and potential redevelopment sites for needed housing types. | Land capacity (required): Analyze infrastructure needs/capacity and, if documented constraints prevent meeting total need, establish the minimum feasible number over 20 years and actions to remove constraints. | Development constraints (required): Analyze zoning, development standards and infrastructure constraints and identify market-based incentives. | Preservation (required): Provide regulations allowing rehabilitation, improvement or development of the needed housing units. | Action program (required): Describe housing actions and implement land-use regulations; identify zoning inconsistencies and schedules to bring regulations/maps into substantial compliance. | Monitoring (required): Document progress toward construction of needed housing at each five-year land-use-plan review; monitor implementation schedules.

name: Rhode Island
housing_duty: Every comprehensive plan must include housing needs analysis, suitable development/rehabilitation areas and an affordable-housing program with goals, actions and timeframes. The state housing strategy is also an element with which local plans must conform.
plan_mandate: Every city and town must prepare, adopt, maintain and implement a comprehensive plan, submit it for state review, and keep zoning consistent with it.
coverage: All cities and towns, without a population cutoff. Affordable-stock thresholds affect comprehensive-permit rules, not the universal housing-element duty.
assessment_detail: The Executive Office of Housing, with the Division of Statewide Planning, prepares the state housing strategy and need forecasts underlying Housing 2030. Cities and towns also analyze existing and forecast local needs. State assessment is relevant because local plans must conform to the adopted State Guide Plan, not merely because state housing research exists.
assessment_method: Housing 2030 uses household-growth scenarios, replacement and affordability analysis. Its municipal production goals use existing stock multiplied by growth-category rates based on jobs and transit, rather than dividing a regional shortage. Local housing forecasts and adequate, valid supporting data remain required by § § 45-22.2-6 and -9.
assessment_local_role: Each municipality prepares its own stock/need analysis. Housing 2030 requires adoption of its respective total and low/moderate-income production goals and a realistic implementation approach in the comprehensive plan. Section 45-22.2-9(f) requires conformity amendments within one year. This planning duty does not guarantee construction.
allocation_authority: Executive Office of Housing sets municipal production benchmarks
allocation_detail: Housing 2030 sets municipality-specific permit goals using annual stock growth of at least 0.4%, 0.6% or 0.8%, depending on jobs/transit category. Affordable rental goals are 10% or 15% of those goals depending on existing affordable stock. These are production benchmarks; municipal goals exceed the statewide total rather than apportioning a fixed regional need. The statutory 10% affordable-stock threshold is a separate permit-law benchmark.
enforcement: The chief of Statewide Planning reviews content, valid data and consistency with the State Guide Plan. Housing 2030 requires revision of municipal plans that lack a realistic path to their production goals. Failure to conform after a guide-plan change may cause loss of state approval. Zoning must conform to the plan. Separate comprehensive-permit incentives vary with affordable stock and qualifying inclusionary zoning.
key_distinction: State assessment and universal local housing planning coexist with stock-based municipal production goals. Those goals are not a California-style apportionment; the pre-2026 alternative urban 15% threshold is not used for the current comprehensive-permit rule.
timing_note: Housing 2030 adopted December 11, 2025; municipal conformity amendments are due within one year under § 45-22.2-9(f).
uncertainties: Municipal implementation of Housing 2030 has not been audited. The record addresses housing-plan obligations and production benchmarks; it does not claim a complete audit of 2026 comprehensive-permit procedures.

name: Delaware
housing_duty: Plans in municipalities above 2,000 population must contain affordable-housing planning. The Housing for Every Delawarean Act now requires a specific affordable housing plan with measurable goals, mandatory zoning actions and a menu of additional strategies.
plan_mandate: An incorporated city or town may establish a planning commission; a commission established under Title 22 chapter 7 must prepare a comprehensive development plan. Municipal charters can impose additional duties.
coverage: Local jurisdictions with population greater than 2,000 that are required to adopt comprehensive plans under Titles 9, 22 or 29. Municipal plans at or below 2,000 still state a position on housing growth, but the new affordable-plan requirement does not apply.
assessment_detail: The legislature specifies a strategic benchmark that 20% of local housing units qualify as affordable. Municipalities develop measurable goals in collaboration with the Delaware State Housing Authority. The reviewed law does not require DSHA or municipalities to calculate a projected housing-need allocation.
assessment_method: The benchmark is a share of housing stock, not a demand forecast. Statutory affordability definitions use income up to 80% AMI for rentals and 120% AMI for ownership; HUD provides AMI. DSHA collaboration is not assignment of regional need.
assessment_local_role: Local jurisdictions formulate goals, timelines and zoning strategies with DSHA, make meaningful measurable progress toward the 20% benchmark, and provide compliance information. No external municipality-specific unit-need estimate was identified.
allocation_authority: Legislature sets stock benchmark; locality sets implementation goals
allocation_detail: Section 9221 establishes a strategic 20% affordable-stock goal and progress duty. No state/regional apportionment of projected need among municipalities appears in § § 9220–9224. DSHA collaborates on plans; it does not allocate a housing-need number.
enforcement: Governor certification checks comprehensive-plan requirements and can return deficient plans for revision. DSHA and the Office of State Planning Coordination must gather compliance information and publish annual progress reports from 2028. Municipal adopted plans have force of law; state infrastructure/financial assistance can be withheld for substantial inconsistency with state development policies.
key_distinction: The July 2026 law uses a 20% stock benchmark and mandated reforms, not a California-style allocation. Its phased first-plan deadlines matter; proposals requiring DSHA approval or a > 10,000 special-housing trigger were not enacted. No parcel inventory or quantified demand forecast is expressly required in the new affordable-plan elements.
timing_note: Law effective July 13, 2026. Initial plan at next comprehensive plan; plans adopted before Feb 1, 2027 defer until next five-year review.

name: South Dakota
housing_duty: Chapter 11-6 does not expressly require a housing component. Section 11-7-53.2 separately requires a municipality-wide housing-needs/program plan triggered by covered project financing; that narrower trigger is outside this inventory’s general-plan classification.
plan_mandate: Section 11-6-2 directs every municipality to provide a planning commission and undertake a comprehensive plan as soon as possible. Section 11-6-3 permits a county commission to serve by contract.
coverage: General planning covers incorporated cities and towns without a population cutoff. No housing-element coverage trigger was identified in Chapter 11-6.
assessment_detail: Chapter 11-6 requires general growth surveys, but specifies no housing-needs assessor. Separately, a housing/redevelopment commission must document municipal housing needs before issuing bonds or obligations for a covered housing-development project.
assessment_method: No housing calculation method is specified for the comprehensive plan. Section 11-7-53.2 requires needs data, proposed methods, target areas and programs for the separate financing approval.
assessment_local_role: Local commissions prepare comprehensive-plan recommendations. Project-financing needs analysis and governing-body approval are separate from the general-plan classification.
allocation_detail: The reviewed planning and project-financing provisions assign no municipal share of state or regional housing need.
enforcement: Chapter 11-6 provides local hearings, council adoption and referendum procedures. Section 11-7-53.2 separately conditions covered project financing on an approved housing-needs plan. No general-plan housing-element certification system was identified.
key_distinction: A mandatory comprehensive plan does not necessarily contain a mandatory housing element. Excluding §11-7-53.2 is a scope judgment based on its project-financing trigger: its required needs/program analysis does cover the municipality. This row does not mean South Dakota has no housing-planning duties.

name: North Dakota
housing_duty: The reviewed municipal planning and zoning chapters do not expressly require a housing element.
plan_mandate: Master-plan establishment is permissive under §40-48-02; an established planning commission must prepare a plan under §40-48-08. City zoning must follow a documented comprehensive plan under §40-47-03.
coverage: Municipal master planning and city zoning; no housing-component population trigger identified.
assessment_detail: General planning studies are required, but no mandatory housing-needs assessor is identified. ND Housing publishes statewide needs research; its existence does not establish an assigned general-plan need number.
assessment_method: The reviewed statutes prescribe no municipal housing-demand formula or incorporation of a state needs estimate.
assessment_local_role: The commission studies local conditions and growth. Voluntary housing analysis is not coded as a state-mandated assessment.
allocation_detail: Neither reviewed municipal chapter assigns state or regional housing-unit shares to cities.
enforcement: Local hearings and adoption procedures govern master plans. Zoning must conform to a documented comprehensive plan. No housing-element certification or fair-share enforcement regime was identified in these chapters.
key_distinction: A zoning-related comprehensive-plan requirement and statewide housing research do not establish a mandatory housing element or municipal needs allocation.

name: Alaska
housing_duty: Effective October 14, 2025, AS 29.40.030(a) expressly includes a housing development plan among the components that a comprehensive plan may include. Housing remains optional.
plan_mandate: First- and second-class boroughs must plan under AS 29.40 and adopt a comprehensive plan. First-class cities outside boroughs have the same planning duty; second-class cities outside boroughs may exercise it. Home-rule boroughs and cities outside boroughs have a general planning duty under separate home-rule provisions.
coverage: The chapter 29.40 framework applies to first-/second-class boroughs and, through AS 29.35.260(c), first-class cities outside boroughs and participating second-class cities outside boroughs. Borough planning is areawide, with authorized delegation to cities. Home-rule planning provisions do not impose the same enumerated chapter 29.40 contents.
assessment_detail: The reviewed planning provisions identify no required housing-need estimate or assessor. The locality may prepare a housing-development plan, but the statute does not prescribe its analytical contents.
assessment_method: No housing-need formula is specified in AS 29.40.030 or the 2025 amendment.
assessment_local_role: The local planning commission recommends and the local governing body adopts the comprehensive plan and any chosen housing component; adoption does not require accommodating a state-assigned housing number under these provisions.
allocation_detail: The enacted optional housing-development-plan item supplies neither an assessment formula nor an external municipal housing-need assignment. No such assignment was identified in the reviewed Title 29 planning framework.
enforcement: For chapter 29.40 jurisdictions, the governing body adopts the comprehensive plan by ordinance and periodically reviews and updates it as necessary. These general planning procedures do not convert the optional housing-development component into a mandatory one.
key_distinction: The 2025 law added optional housing planning, not a mandatory housing element. Borough/city class and home-rule status matter more than population cutoffs.
timing_note: SB 50 became chapter 19 SLA 2025, effective October 14, 2025. The official downloadable Title 29 compilation read on September 20, 2026 omitted its housing addition, so the enacted amendment and official bill history control this record.

name: Vermont
housing_duty: An adopted municipal plan must include a housing element addressing the needs and targets identified by its regional planning commission. Act 179 expanded its contents effective July 1, 2026.
plan_mandate: Municipal comprehensive planning is authorized, not universally compelled, by 24 V.S.A. § 4381. A municipality choosing a plan must meet § 4382; regional approval has additional compatibility requirements.
coverage: Municipal plans statewide, without a population cutoff. The mandate is conditional on undertaking the municipal planning program; regional planning commissions separately must assess regional and community needs.
assessment_detail: The Department of Housing and Community Development publishes statewide and regional housing targets or ranges in the Statewide Housing Needs Assessment. Regional planning commissions then assess housing investments and disaggregate regional targets among municipalities, using demographic, stock and local studies.
assessment_method: Section 4348a(a)(9) specifies affordability, price, quality, size/type and zoning-district considerations. DHCD supplies the initial state/regional targets; RPCs perform the community-level assessment and disaggregation. The statute does not prescribe a single mathematical municipal formula.
assessment_local_role: The municipality supplies local housing information and writes actions responsive to its RPC target. It analyzes regulatory, labor and physical constraints and documents progress when amending or readopting its plan; local plan authorship does not make it the initial need assessor.
allocation_authority: Regional planning commissions, from DHCD targets
allocation_detail: RPCs must disaggregate the state regional housing targets or ranges by municipality. Municipal housing elements must address those RPC needs and targets. This is externally assigned planning need, without a statutory guarantee of construction or California-style housing-element certification.
enforcement: RPC approval checks required elements and compatibility with the regional plan; confirmation requires an approved plan and active implementation. Confirmation brings planning funds and impact-fee authority. These mechanisms do not convert the target into a municipal construction obligation.
key_distinction: Municipal plans are optional, but their housing elements respond to external targets. The 2026 session law adds requirements missing from the displayed 2025 code compilation.
timing_note: Expanded housing-element contents effective July 1, 2026; online § 4382 alone omits this amendment.

name: Wyoming
housing_duty: The municipal master-plan article does not expressly require a housing element, housing-needs assessment or equivalent municipality-wide housing strategy.
plan_mandate: A city or town may establish a planning commission. The commission must prepare and adopt a master plan after public hearings; the governing body may adopt the master plan. The reviewed article does not impose a universal municipal comprehensive-plan adoption duty.
coverage: Reviewed scope: cities and towns under Title 15, chapter 1, article 5. Commission planning beyond municipal boundaries requires county-planning concurrence. No housing-specific population trigger is stated in these sections.
assessment_detail: The reviewed municipal planning provisions require general surveys of conditions and probable future growth, but specify no required housing-demand calculation or housing assessor.
assessment_method: General careful and comprehensive surveys under § 15-1-504; no housing-need method or formula identified in the reviewed article.
assessment_local_role: An established local planning commission surveys and prepares the master plan, and the governing body may adopt it. No externally assigned housing estimate must be accommodated under these provisions.
allocation_detail: No state or regional municipal housing-need allocation was identified in the reviewed municipal planning article. Statewide housing studies and individual housing programs are not coded as an allocation controlling local general plans.
enforcement: The article provides public hearings, commission certification and optional governing-body adoption. After adoption, certain public facilities require commission review for conformity, subject to governing-body override. No housing-element certification or housing-number compliance mechanism was identified in this article.
key_distinction: A general zoning plan, population-density recommendations and slum-area replanning are listed master-plan subjects, but they do not expressly require a housing-needs element or sites inventory.
